added.title: Senior Perception AI Engineer - Autonomous Vehicles
added.description:
Requirements

Self-driving cars need to understand the road ahead in real time, even without a prior map. Our team builds the online mapping system that turns raw data from multiple sensors into an accurate, continuously updated 3D model of the driving environment. This model captures lanes, road boundaries, crosswalks, intersection layouts, and traffic control information to support decisions across the autonomous driving system. You’ll write the models, write the C++, and ship both into vehicles on the road, running on NVIDIA DRIVE Orin and Thor. The tasks you perform will be tested at scale, on real cars, with real safety requirements. NVIDIA’s autonomous driving stack spans the full range of automation, and online mapping is a core component across it, so your work will reach L2++, L3, and L4 systems. The role spans two subject areas, and we want someone who enjoys both:

Learned mapping involves training DNNs to predict map elements directly from visual sensors, laser scanning, and radar. This includes owning the GT story and collaborating with partners to provide the vital data.
Geometry and C++ engineering: building the post-processing that turns network outputs into stable, consistent, production-ready map elements.

What You’ll Be Doing

Design, train, and improve PyTorch models that predict online map elements (lanes, road boundaries, crosswalks, road markings, topology) from camera, LiDAR, and/or radar, using BEV and vectorized-map representations.
Solve the hardest scenes: model intersection topology (connectivity between incoming and outgoing lanes, turn paths, merges and splits) and traffic light understanding (detection, state, and association of each light to the lanes it controls).
Write production C++ for geometry-based post-processing: curve and surface fitting, association, multi-frame fusion and tracking, topology reasoning, and consistency checks on DNN outputs.
Apply multi-view geometry, calibration, coordinate transforms, and sensor fusion to produce 3D maps that stay accurate and stable over time.
Optimize and deploy models alongside algorithms on NVIDIA DRIVE Orin and Thor under real-time and safety constraints, and get them running in vehicles.
Lead the narrative around GT and the data loop by planning datasets and defining GT and labeling requirements. Work with labeling, data, and tooling partners to produce high-quality GT. Mine data, choose metrics, and analyze failure cases to drive improvements.
Define critical metrics and build evaluation tooling to measure quality gains against large-scale real-world data.
Partner with perception, localization, planning, and infrastructure teams to integrate online mapping into the full AV stack, across L2++, L3, and L4 programs.
Contribute to technical direction and architecture decisions across the learned and geometric components of the mapping system.

What We Need To See

MS or PhD or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent experience
5+ years of industry or research experience in autonomous driving, robotics, or computer vision.
Strong foundation in 3D geometry: camera models, projective geometry, coordinate transforms, optimization, and curve/surface fitting.
Strong C++ skills, with a track record of designing and shipping production-quality algorithm code that is fast, reliable, and maintainable.
Hands-on experience training deep neural networks in PyTorch, including model design, training pipelines, debugging, and performance analysis.
Experience with data-driven development: building datasets, defining labels and GT, choosing metrics, and improving models by analyzing failures.
Excellent problem-solving and communication skills, and the ability to drive technical direction across teams.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Direct experience with DNN-based online or HD map generation, or BEV perception (e.g., vectorized map prediction, lane topology learning), or equivalent experience to BEV perception.
Experience with intersection understanding, such as lane connectivity and topology reasoning in sophisticated junctions, or traffic light detection and lane association.
Experience combining learned models with geometric post-processing in a production AV system and publications or open-source contributions in 3D vision, mapping, or autonomous driving.
Background in sensor fusion, multi-object tracking, or temporal fusion for map elements.
Experience deploying DNNs and algorithms on embedded GPUs (CUDA, TensorRT), ideally on DRIVE Orin or Thor, under real-time constraints.

added.description:
About Checkr

Checkr is building the data platform to power safe and fair decisions. Over 140,000 companies and millions of people rely on Checkr for AI verification in the moments that matter most: getting a new job, a new place to live, a car ride, childcare, even a date. Customers include Uber, Pennymac, Airbnb, Doordash, and Anthropic.

We’re a team that thrives on solving complex problems with innovative solutions that advance our mission. Checkr is recognized on Forbes Cloud 100 2025 List and is a Y Combinator 2024 Breakthrough Company.

About The Team/role

We’re hiring an ML Engineer (P3) to build and ship the AI systems that power Checkr’s core products. This role sits on the ML team inside Checkr’s Data & ML organization within Engineering.

Checkr runs millions of background checks a year. The ML team builds the systems that make those checks faster, more accurate, and cheaper to operate: document processing, charge classification, entity resolution, and in-product intelligence. These are production services that Product Engineering depends on daily.

This is not a research role or a notebook role. You’ll own ML services end-to-end: design them, code them, deploy them, monitor them. We need someone who writes production software, builds with LLMs and APIs as first-class tools, and can tell the difference between working code and AI slop. If you’ve spent the last few years building AI-native software and you care deeply about engineering craft, we want to talk.

This role sits in the central Data & ML team within the Engineering organization. You will partner daily with Product Engineering, Product, and cross-functional teams. You’ll also contribute to Checkr’s broader AI strategy, including our initiative to deploy our agentic fleet and build scalable context with our semantic layer.

We are looking for someone based in San Francisco who has built ML systems in fast-moving, impact-first environments. Less process, more shipping. Less paperwork, more results.

What You’ll Do

Build and deploy ML/AI services. Design, develop, and ship ML models and AI systems that Product Engineering teams rely on. You write the model code, the API layer, the monitoring, and the tests. Not notebooks; production services.
Design with LLMs and APIs. Use LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) as building blocks in production systems. You know when to call an LLM, when to fine-tune, when to use a classical model, and when to write a rule. You think about cost, latency, and quality together.
Ship production software. Write clean, well-structured code with solid OOP, proper abstractions, error handling, and tests. Your code gets reviewed by SWEs and passes. CI/CD is how you work, not something you bolt on at the end.
Partner with product and engineering. Translate business problems into ML solutions. Define API contracts with product engineers. Explain your approach clearly to non-ML partners and leave the room with alignment, not confusion.
Evaluate and iterate fast. Build evaluation frameworks, run experiments, and make data-driven decisions about model and system performance. Ship and iterate; don’t wait for perfect.
Ship AI-powered workflows. Put AI to work on your own processes: automate pipelines, build agentic workflows, and contribute reusable skills and context to Checkr’s agentic platform. The expectation is that our teams operate AI-first.

What You Bring

A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, or a related technical field, or equivalent depth from experience
6+ years building software professionally, with at least 2 of those building ML systems that run in production
Strong Python fluency; you write clean, testable, well-structured code with solid OOP instincts. Hands-on experience using LLM APIs in production systems: prompt engineering, structured outputs, function calling, cost management, and evaluation
You’ve built and maintained APIs, worked with CI/CD pipelines, and shipped code that other engineers depend on
Comfort with and enthusiasm for AI-assisted workflows; experience using LLMs, code-generation tools, or agentic systems in production or operational contexts is a strong signal
You use AI tools (Copilot, Claude, etc.) to move faster, but you understand every line they produce. You can spot AI slop and you don’t ship it
An A-player mindset with a strong bias for action: you raise the bar, move with urgency, stay resilient through ambiguity, and take ownership to deliver meaningful outcomes.

Nice to have

Experience with MLOps platforms (MLflow, SageMaker, Vertex, or similar)
Background in document processing, OCR, or information extraction
Experience with PySpark or large-scale data processing
Ruby experience (Checkr’s platform runs on Rails)
Familiarity with compliance-sensitive domains (fintech, legal tech, HR tech)
Working knowledge of dbt, Snowflake, or modern ELT/data transformation tools

added.title: Senior AI Engineer
added.description:
The Problem

We're building an agentic AI caregiver advocate that lives in your text messages and acts on behalf of rare disease patients and their families. It doesn't just answer questions. It makes phone calls to insurance companies, automates browser sessions to find clinical trials, prepares patients for specialist appointments using their complete medical history, navigates government benefits applications, and coordinates across multiple sub-agents to get things done. It maintains persistent memory across months of interactions and gets smarter about each patient's condition, care team, and needs over time.

The AI engineering challenge: build an autonomous agent that operates reliably in one of the highest-stakes domains imaginable — where a wrong answer about a medication interaction or a missed insurance deadline has real consequences for a sick child and their family. Traditional chatbot architecture doesn't cut it. We need engineers who can design agentic systems that reason, plan, use tools, and know when to escalate to a human.

The Role

We're hiring AI Engineers to build the intelligence behind our AI advocate. You'll design and implement the agentic LLM systems, RAG pipelines, tool-use frameworks, and evaluation infrastructure that make it effective, reliable, and safe. This is not a research role — you'll ship production systems that real patients depend on daily.

You'll work closely with Product, Platform Engineering, and clinical advisors. You'll report to the CTO.

What You'll Build

Agentic orchestration
— Design and implement the multi-agent architecture that powers our advocate's ability to reason, plan, and execute complex multi-step tasks (scheduling appointments, filing insurance appeals, researching treatment options) with appropriate guardrails and human-in-the-loop checkpoints.

RAG and medical knowledge systems
— Build retrieval pipelines over patient medical records, condition-specific knowledge bases, and community-sourced data from 125+ rare disease communities. Ensure the advocate's responses are grounded in the patient's actual medical history, not generic information.

Tool-use and integrations
— Build and maintain the frameworks that let our agent take real-world actions: browser automation, phone calls, form filling, document generation, and API integrations with healthcare systems. Each tool-use needs to be reliable, auditable, and scoped to the right permissions.

Conversation intelligence
— Design the systems that make the advocate's WhatsApp conversations feel natural, contextual, and proactive. This includes long-term memory, conversation state management, personalization, and knowing when to surface information the patient didn't ask for but needs.

Evaluation and safety
— Build evaluation frameworks for agentic outputs in a domain where "good enough" isn't good enough. Develop testing infrastructure for multi-step agent workflows, hallucination detection, medical accuracy validation, and regression testing across model updates.

Prompt engineering and model optimization
— Design prompt architectures that balance capability, cost, and latency. Evaluate and integrate new models as the landscape evolves. Optimize inference costs — our unit economics depend on it.

Who You Are

You've built LLM-powered systems that went to production and had real users — not just demos and prototypes. You understand that the hard part of agentic AI isn't getting a cool demo working, it's making it reliable at the 95th percentile. You've dealt with the unglamorous parts: evaluation frameworks, prompt regression testing, cost optimization, and edge cases that only show up at scale.

You care about the craft of building AI systems, not just the hype cycle. You've formed opinions about when to use agents vs. chains vs. simple prompts, and you can articulate the tradeoffs. You're comfortable working in a startup where the stack is evolving fast and the best architecture for next quarter might not be the one you built last quarter.

Must-Have Skills

4+ years of software engineering experience, with 2+ years building LLM-powered applications in production.
Strong proficiency in Python and hands-on experience with agentic AI frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, or equivalent).
Experience designing and implementing RAG systems — including chunking strategies, embedding models, vector databases, retrieval evaluation, and hybrid search.
Track record building AI systems that take real-world actions (tool-use, function calling, browser automation, API orchestration), not just generate text.
Strong software engineering fundamentals — you write production-grade code with tests, logging, error handling, and clear abstractions. You're an engineer who uses AI, not a prompt writer who avoids code.
Experience with evaluation and testing of LLM systems — you've built evals, measured hallucination rates, and designed regression suites for non-deterministic outputs.
Comfort with ambiguity and fast iteration. You've worked at a startup or early-stage company and thrived.
Strong written and verbal communication — you can explain agentic architecture tradeoffs to a PM and debug a prompt chain with an engineer in the same afternoon.

Preferred Skills

Experience with healthcare, life sciences, or other regulated domains where AI output accuracy has high stakes (HIPAA compliance, clinical data handling).
Familiarity with multi-agent architectures — designing systems where multiple specialized agents collaborate, hand off tasks, and share context.
Experience with WhatsApp Business API, messaging platforms, or conversational AI at scale.
Background in inference cost optimization — model selection, caching, batching, routing between models of different capability/cost profiles.
Familiarity with medical data formats (FHIR, HL7, CDA) or experience building systems over medical records.
Experience with voice AI, telephony APIs, or browser automation frameworks (Playwright, Puppeteer).
Contributions to open-source AI/LLM tooling or active engagement with the agentic AI community.

Who We Are

Citizen Health was founded on the belief — shaped by firsthand lived experiences navigating healthcare — that having the right advocate is the single most important factor in achieving better care and outcomes. By uniquely combining data, AI, and community, Citizen is building a personalized AI advocate powered by patients' complete medical histories and data from thousands of other patients to generate personalized insights for clinical decisions and day-to-day challenges. Starting in rare and complex conditions, patients share their data in exchange for value, enabling biopharma and researchers with seamless access to patients and regulatory-grade data, shaving years off drug development for much-needed treatments.

Citizen is founded by experienced entrepreneurs with multiple successes under their belts and is funded by top-tier investors including 8VC, Transformation Capital, and Headline Ventures, among others. We are a mission-driven team excited to be building the future of consumer healthcare.

Why Join Us

Build an agentic AI system in production that actually helps people — not another chatbot, not a copilot for knowledge workers, but an autonomous advocate for families navigating rare diseases.
Work on problems at the frontier of agentic AI: multi-step planning in high-stakes domains, tool-use over messy real-world systems, long-term memory and personalization, evaluation of non-deterministic autonomous agents.
Ship to real users immediately. Our AI advocate is live and serving patients today. Your code will be in production within your first sprint.
A fast-paced, high-growth setting with expanding opportunities and clear paths for career progression.
A supportive culture of learning, experimentation, and innovation, where new ideas are encouraged and explored.

Compensation & Benefits

Competitive salary + equity
Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance
Unlimited PTO, including 12 weeks paid parental leave
Flexible remote-first work environment
Work-from-anywhere 30 days per year
Company offsites

Our Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion:
Citizen Health is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. Everyone deserves an equal chance to contribute and grow here — regardless of race, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status.

Don't meet every qualification?
No worries! We believe that passion, curiosity, and the right mindset are just as important as a checklist of skills. If you’re excited about what we’re building, we encourage you to apply.

Compensation Range: $150K - $300K

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience

Join a high-velocity team with deep startup roots. You get the autonomy of a small team, backed by Salesforce's Data Cloud and security infrastructure, to build a 0-to-1 product at global scale.

Global supply chains still run on email, spreadsheets, and fragmented data. The economy moves fast; supply chains don't. That gap sits on top of the $13T of goods shipped annually, one of the largest untapped opportunities in enterprise software.

You’ll train both foundation models and customer-specific models that predict and improve how users engage, click, and convert, and you’ll own each model’s lifecycle end to end: from initial idea, through research and training, to the infrastructure that deploys it.

You’re a great fit if you have:

Experience fine-tuning vision-language models (VLMs) or large language models (LLMs)
Experience training ranking, click-through rate (CTR), conversion, or engagement models
Strong ML infrastructure experience, including training pipelines, data systems, and model serving
The ability to own models end to end, from research and experimentation to production deployment
Strong software engineering fundamentals and experience shipping reliable production systems
The ability to translate business metrics into modeling objectives and rigorous evaluations
Curiosity, pragmatism, and excitement about working on problems with no established playbook
A track record of exceptional achievement, whether in industry, research, or academics
Experience building agent loops, edge or low-latency model serving, and working with e-commerce, growth, or experimentation teams

What you’ll do:

Build foundation models and customer-specific models for performance optimization
Fine-tune VLMs and LLMs to understand and improve digital experiences
Train ranking, CTR, conversion, and engagement models that guide what Coframe generates and ships
Own the full model lifecycle, from idea and research through training, evaluation, and deployment
Build and scale the ML infrastructure for training, serving, and monitoring models in production
Develop online and offline evaluation systems that tie model performance to real customer outcomes
Build feedback loops that let models continuously improve from real-world experiment results
Work with technical and non-technical teams to turn customer goals into models, metrics, and product improvements

Benefits:

Flexible (Unlimited) Paid Time Off
Top-of-the-line Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits for you and your family
Life Insurance and Disability Benefits
401k Plan with Coframe match
All meals fully covered in-office
Gym membership

Why Coframe:

Elite Team:
Our founder is a serial entrepreneur who previously co-founded a $2B+ unicorn with Tom Brady and guest lectures AI at Stanford. Our team includes researchers from top institutions who created some of the world's most popular open-source code generation projects.

OpenAI:
We’re the only marketing technology company officially partnered with OpenAI. Our engineers and researchers work directly with their team to co-train a model specifically for our use case, which is a differentiator, and a testament to the technical caliber of our team.

We’re currently growing at 120% QoQ with a consistent flood of inbound demand. We’re looking for the right saleshumans to capture this demand and market opportunity.

We’re backed by tier-1 investors including Khosla Ventures, Nat Friedman (former GitHub CEO), and Rich Miner (Android co-founder). Joining now means getting a seat on the rocket ship before our Series A: a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to join in the early innings.

We effectively 10x testing velocity, replacing agencies, legacy tools, and the need to pull in-house designers and engineers for testing. In the last 6 months, we have already driven $221.4M in incremental revenue for our customers like Dropbox, Replit, and Intuit.

added.title: Sr. Software Engineer, Agentic
added.description:
About The Role

Agentic Pods is pioneering a new way for Engineering to partner with teams across Uber and transform how work gets done through AI. Our engineers embed directly with operational teams to understand complex workflows, reimagine what's possible with agentic AI, and build production-grade systems that turn those opportunities into reality.

We are looking for an Agentic Software Engineer to design, build, and operate intelligent, reliable agentic systems that transform complex operational workflows at scale.

This role sits at the intersection of backend engineering, production reliability, and applied AI, combining strong technical ownership with a forward-deployed engineering approach. You'll work closely with operators and domain experts to identify high-impact opportunities, determine where AI agents can safely and effectively improve workflows, and translate ambiguous business challenges into scalable, production-ready solutions.

You'll own the full engineering lifecycle, from problem discovery and system architecture to implementation, deployment, and continuous improvement. This is an opportunity to shape how Uber applies agentic AI to real-world operations while helping establish the technical foundations for broader adoption across the company.

What You'll Do

Design and Build Agentic Systems

Partner directly with operational teams to understand complex workflows, identify inefficiencies, and determine where AI agents, traditional automation, or human decision-making can deliver meaningful improvements.
Design, develop, and deploy production-grade agentic systems, including AI agents, reusable skills, backend services, APIs, system integrations, data pipelines, and human-in-the-loop workflows.
Rapidly prototype, validate, and iterate on solutions with real users, translating ambiguous requirements into reliable, scalable software.

Own Production Reliability and Performance

Design systems with reliability, scalability, and operational resilience in mind, establishing clear performance and quality standards.
Build comprehensive observability across agent behavior, model outputs, system dependencies, and workflow outcomes using tracing, logging, metrics, monitoring, and alerting.
Own systems throughout their production lifecycle, troubleshooting failures, implementing recovery mechanisms, and continuously improving performance based on operational insights and user feedback.

Build Safe, Measurable, and Trustworthy AI Systems

Develop evaluation frameworks to measure agent effectiveness, including task completion, output quality, tool selection, policy compliance, and failure handling.
Implement testing and validation strategies across development, controlled rollouts, and production environments to ensure consistent and predictable system behavior.
Design appropriate safeguards, including access controls, human approvals, auditability, data protection, reversible actions, and escalation mechanisms.
Collaborate with Security, Privacy, Legal, and Data teams to ensure AI-powered workflows meet Uber's standards for safety, compliance, and operational integrity.

Drive Reusability and Engineering Excellence

Identify opportunities to transform individual solutions into reusable agent capabilities, shared services, platform components, and standardized integration patterns.
Design flexible architectures that support different business needs and regional requirements without unnecessary duplication.
Contribute to engineering standards, architecture decisions, development tooling, deployment practices, and reliability frameworks that enable Agentic Pods to scale effectively across Uber.

Who Thrives On This Team

We're looking for engineers who combine strong software engineering fundamentals with curiosity, ownership, and a passion for applying emerging technologies to real-world challenges.

Agentic-first thinker: You see beyond existing workflows and recognize opportunities to fundamentally improve how work gets done using AI and automation.
0→1 builder: You thrive in ambiguous environments and can turn loosely defined problems into working, production-ready solutions.
Product-minded engineer: You focus on solving meaningful user problems and understand that the best solution isn't always the most technically complex.
Systems thinker: You balance immediate business needs with long-term scalability, reliability, and opportunities for reuse.
Collaborative problem solver: You learn unfamiliar domains quickly, build strong relationships with stakeholders, and communicate effectively across technical and non-technical teams.

Minimum Qualifications

PhD or equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field; or 3 years of full-time software engineering experience, including 2 years of specialized technical software engineering experience in one or more programming languages, such as C, C++, Java, Python, or Go.

Note: The 2 years of specialized software engineering experience may be gained through education, full-time employment, additional training, coursework, research, or a combination of these. This experience is not necessarily in addition to the education and full-time work experience requirements listed above.

Strong experience designing, developing, and deploying production backend or distributed systems, such as AI-enabled applications, orchestration platforms, APIs, asynchronous workflows, developer platforms, or enterprise integrations.
Hands-on experience owning production systems, including monitoring, alerting, incident response, troubleshooting, failure recovery, and debugging across application, infrastructure, and data dependencies.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on experience building agentic AI applications or integrating large language models (LLMs) with tools, APIs, enterprise data sources, and permissioned systems.
Familiarity with agent orchestration, evaluation frameworks, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), context management, model routing, and AI safety controls.
Experience in site reliability engineering (SRE), infrastructure, platform engineering, production engineering, or forward-deployed engineering environments.
Experience designing and operating systems that support sensitive, business-critical, or operationally consequential workflows.
Demonstrated ability to contribute to technical design, make sound architectural decisions, and collaborate across engineering teams.
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work directly with business stakeholders to translate complex operational challenges into technical solutions.

For San Francisco, CA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $202,000 per year - USD $224,000 per year.

For Sunnyvale, CA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $202,000 per year - USD $224,000 per year.

For all US locations, you will be eligible to participate in Uber's bonus program, and may be offered an equity award & other types of comp. All full-time employees are eligible to participate in a 401(k) plan. You will also be eligible for various benefits.

Ready to Ride?

This isn't the kind of place where you follow a playbook — it's where you help write one. If you're driven by impact, energized by challenge, and ready to shape how the world moves — we'd love to hear from you.

You may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and other compensation, as well as a range of benefits. Explore our benefits.

Offices remain key to collaboration and Uber's culture. Unless approved for full remote work, employees must spend at least 50% of their time in-office. Some roles, like those at greenlight hubs, require full-time in-office presence. Ask your Recruiter for details about this role's requirements.

Uber is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. added.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Production
added.description:
About David AI

David AI is the first audio data research company. We bring an R&D approach to data–developing datasets with the same rigor AI labs bring to models. Our mission is to bring AI into the real world, and we believe audio is the gateway. Speech is versatile, accessible, and human—it fits naturally into everyday life. As audio AI advances and new use cases emerge, high-quality training data is the bottleneck. This is where David AI comes in.

David AI was founded in 2024 by a team of former Scale AI engineers and operators. In less than a year, we've brought on most FAANG companies and AI labs as customers. We recently raised a $50M Series B from Meritech, NVIDIA, Jack Altman (Alt Capital), Amplify Partners, First Round Capital and other Tier 1 investors.

Our team is sharp, humble, ambitious, and tight-knit. We're looking for the best research, engineering, product, and operations minds to join us on our mission to push the frontier of audio AI.

About Our Engineering Team

At David AI, our engineers build the pipelines, platforms, and models that transform raw audio into high-signal data for leading AI labs and enterprises. We're a tight-knit team of product engineers, infrastructure specialists, and machine learning experts focused on building the world's first audio data research company.

We move fast, own our work end-to-end, and ship to production daily. Our team designs real-time pipelines handling terabytes of speech data and deploys cutting-edge generative audio models.

About This Role

We generate audio data for the world’s leading speech and audio labs. Data only matters if it makes a customer’s model measurably better, and finding out whether it does is your job. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, Production, you’ll own the loop between a customer’s model, our research team, and our data production. In a typical week you’ll run an ablation on Monday, see a signal on Tuesday, change how we collect data on Wednesday, and ship a recommendation that makes it to the customer by Friday. You’ll be shipping something on the order of days, not weeks.

This role is for someone who is equally comfortable in a codebase, translating customer requirements into how we produce data, and in the details of how we ship product features to yield data that improves our customers’ models. You’ll care about why a model regressed, and also about which recording setup, product experience, or automated QA step caused it.

In this role, you will

Run the daily experiment loop. Turn customer questions into fast, rigorous experiments, get results in days, and iterate until the answer is clear enough to act on.
Design ablations and benchmarks that change decisions. Work with our research engineers to isolate what drives model behavior. Then translate the results into concrete changes in what we collect, how we collect it, and how we filter and weight it.
Develop operational intuition for data quality. Get close to how our data is produced, including recording conditions, contributor pools, annotation, and QA, so you can trace model outcomes back to operational causes and fix them at the source.
Build the tooling that makes speed possible. Ship the eval harnesses, pipelines, and analysis tools that make the next experiment faster than the last, across every customer.
Close the loop with the model improvement lifecycle. Make sure what you learn changes what we produce, so our data keeps improving the models that depend on it.
Shape how we work. Help define our experimentation practices, engineering culture, and roadmap as the team grows.

Your background looks like

added.title: Software Engineer, AI-Powered Software Assurance
added.description:
Responsibilities

We build an internal software assurance platform that helps engineering and security teams analyze source code, assess vulnerabilities and evaluate compliance requirements.

The platform combines agentic AI workflows with code-analysis tools to investigate complex codebases and produce actionable, evidence-backed findings. We focus on deep code understanding across languages, rigorous measurement of analysis quality, and reliable execution at production scale.
We are looking for a hands-on software engineer who can expand these workflows’ analytical capabilities and build the reliable, scalable services that run them.

Build and improve agentic workflows. Develop orchestration, tool integrations, context retrieval, state management and recovery mechanisms for multi-step software assurance investigations. Develop deep, multi-language code analysis. Build tools that navigate large repositories, trace control and data flows, resolve cross-file references and dependencies, and connect evidence across files, services and languages. Combine LLM reasoning with deterministic analysis where appropriate. Measure output quality rigorously. Build representative evaluation datasets, expert-reviewed reference cases and repeatable evaluation pipelines. Measure precision, recall, false-positive and false-negative rates, evidence correctness and task completion. Use held-out cases to assess generalization, and maintain separation between development and evaluation datasets to reduce evaluation leakage. Drive evidence-based improvements. Investigate failure cases, then refine prompts, tools, retrieval and orchestration. Demonstrate measurable improvements through controlled comparisons and regression evaluations.

Responsibilities
- Build scalable, production-grade services. Develop APIs, execution workers, job scheduling and result management that support concurrent workloads, durable execution, retries, cancellation and tenant isolation.
- Improve performance and efficiency. Remove bottlenecks in repository processing, tool execution, context management and model calls. Balance analysis quality against latency, throughput and inference cost.
- Make results observable and auditable. Capture execution traces, tool activity and supporting evidence so teams can reproduce findings and diagnose failures.
- Design secure agent execution. Treat repository content and model outputs as untrusted. Working with the security and infrastructure teams, implement tool permissions, sandboxing and data-handling boundaries.
- Own features through production. Write tested, maintainable code, contribute to design reviews, work with platform engineers on deployment, and investigate production issues.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications
- Significant experience building backend software or distributed systems, including ownership of production services. Strong Python skills and working proficiency in at least one more language, such as Go, Java, Kotlin, TypeScript/JavaScript, C/C++ or Rust.
- Hands-on experience building agentic or LLM-powered applications, including tool use, orchestration, retrieval and systematic failure analysis.
- Ability to understand large, unfamiliar codebases and reason about application behavior, control flow, data flow and dependencies across multiple languages.
- Familiarity with code-analysis techniques such as abstract syntax trees, symbol resolution, call graphs, static analysis or language-server tooling.
- Experience evaluating AI systems or other systems with imperfect outputs, including dataset design, meaningful quality metrics and regression testing.
- Solid backend fundamentals (APIs, queues, persistence, concurrency, idempotency and failure recovery), along with automated testing and CI/CD.
- Hands-on experience building, deploying and debugging containerized services on Kubernetes, including resource configuration, health checks and troubleshooting failed workloads. Ability to communicate uncertainty clearly, separate supported findings from speculation, and work with domain experts to validate results.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience in application security, vulnerability research, secure code review, software quality or compliance analysis.
- Familiarity with LangGraph or comparable agent-orchestration frameworks.
- Experience with compiler tooling, Tree-sitter, CodeQL, Semgrep, or code-search and indexing systems; familiarity with analysis-result formats such as SARIF.
- Experience evaluating retrieval quality, tool-call correctness and multi-step agent behavior. Familiarity with prompt-injection defenses, agent sandboxing and secure handling of proprietary source code.
- Experience with Helm and GitOps-based delivery using Argo CD.
- Experience with Redis, including high-availability setups with Redis Sentinel.
- Experience with OpenTelemetry, LLM gateways or model-serving systems.

TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC is dedicated to the safety and security of millions of Americans who create, discover, and connect with what they love on the apps we operate. USDS Joint Venture helps ensure Americans can continue to express their creativity, discover new hobbies and interests, and build thriving communities and businesses on a global scale.​

Inspiring creativity is at the core of TikTok's mission. Our innovative product is built to help people authentically express themselves, discover and connect – and our global, diverse teams make that possible. Every challenge is an opportunity to learn and innovate as one team. We're resilient and embrace challenges as they come. added.title: Quantum Computing - Senior Applied Research Scientist - Tensor Networks, Research & Delivery _Products & Platforms
added.description:
The Team

Innovation & Delivery Transformation is an organization within Deloitte Consulting that manages a portfolio of emerging technology investments spanning multiple time horizons. Our mission is to accelerate the next generation of technology-driven Consulting offerings. The Quantum Computing team will drive the ecosystem, capability and solution development to drive the impact of quantum technologies across all industries and clients we serve, with the aim of establishing Deloitte as a thought leader and Firm of choice for transformative and disruptive quantum technology.

Position Summary

Do you have a passion for innovation and emerging technologies, along with deep expertise in quantum-inspired algorithms, tensor networks, and high-performance computing? Would you like to be part of the development of a new firm offering? We are currently seeking an experienced Senior Applied Research Scientist - Tensor Networks
to help deliver advanced computational solutions for mission-relevant problems.

As Senior Research Scientist within the Research & Delivery workstream, you will contribute to research and development of advanced computational methods for national security applications. You will investigate how tensor networks can advance modeling, simulation, uncertainty quantification, and decision-making for complex systems. Working with researchers, engineers, and national security specialists, you will translate mission needs into mathematical problems, develop new algorithms, and establish where these methods deliver measurable improvements in accuracy, computational cost, or scale.

You will identify high-value, mission-relevant problems, formulate them for analysis, develop and optimize algorithms, and build rigorous, reproducible benchmarks that distinguish evidence from speculation. You will provide technical contributions to government proposal writing. You will translate validated research into prototypes, reusable software assets, technical roadmaps, and client recommendations while mentoring colleagues and raising standards for technical rigor, reproducibility, and communication.

This role requires candidates to possess or be willing to seek, obtain, and maintain a U.S. government security clearance, as required for the work.

Recruiting for this role ends on 12/31/26.

Work You'll Do

Help build a research practice that extends tensor network methods beyond their established applications to address computational challenges in national security. You will work with researchers, engineers, and mission specialists to identify promising problems, develop new methods, and translate research into capabilities that can be evaluated and used.

Work with national security and domain specialists to translate mission challenges into mathematical models and computational problems. Potential research areas include uncertainty quantification, rare-event analysis, resilient infrastructure and supply chains, probabilistic inference, and dynamical systems.
Determine how dependencies, correlations, network topology, and tensor representations affect computational cost and accuracy. Identify when tensor network approaches are promising and where their limitations arise.
Design, implement, and optimize quantum-inspired algorithms, including tensor network, Pauli-propagation, dequantized, Ising, and QUBO-based methods, using high-performance computing and GPU resources where appropriate.
Collaborate with engineers to improve performance on CPU, GPU, and high-performance computing platforms.
Contribute technical expertise to government proposals and collaborations.
Move validated research from proof of concept to prototype to reusable product assets, including solver and simulator libraries, experiment frameworks, benchmarks, and engineering requirements, in partnership with product and engineering teams.
Serve as technical subject-matter expert in client discussions, executive briefings, proposals, demonstrations, and ecosystem collaborations, clearly communicating results, limitations, uncertainty, and risks.
Mentor researchers and engineers, provide constructive technical review, and establish standards for research rigor, reproducibility, software quality, and communication.
Support work involving government agencies, national laboratories, academic groups, vendors, and other clearance-sensitive stakeholders in accordance with applicable clearance and information-handling requirements.

Required Skills:

Doctoral degree in Physics, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Quantum Information Science, Electrical Engineering, Operations Research, or a related field.
Possess or be willing to seek, obtain, and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.
5+ years of relevant research or development experience, including independently leading technically complex work from problem framing through analysis and communication of conclusions.
Expertise in tensor network methods such as matrix product state (MPS), density matrix renormalization group (DMRG), time-evolving block decimation (TEBD), projected entangled pair states (PEPS), tree tensor networks, or tensor train decompositions, including bond-dimension control, truncation-error analysis, and contraction-path optimization.
Strong foundation in numerical methods, optimization, randomized numerical linear algebra, and quantum-inspired methods for machine learning.
Ability to formulate real-world problems and assess when structural characteristics, such as low entanglement, low rank, sparsity, or operator locality make them suitable for quantum-inspired approaches.
Demonstrated ability to design fair and rigorous benchmarks using strong baselines, appropriate tuning, controlled compute budgets, transparent metrics, and honest reporting of positive and negative results.
Strong Python skills, with experience implementing, reproducing, or critically evaluating algorithms using scientific and quantum software such as NumPy, SciPy, JAX, PyTorch, Quimb, ITensor, Cotengra, Qiskit, Cirq, or PennyLane.
Ability to translate technical research into client-relevant insights, business value, prototypes, roadmaps, or offering priorities.
Publications, preprints, open-source contributions, community benchmarks, conference presentations, or other evidence of technical contribution in quantum-inspired computing, tensor networks, classical simulation, or optimization.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical findings, uncertainty, tradeoffs, and recommendations to technical and business audiences.
Demonstrated ability to guide collaborators, provide constructive technical feedback, and work across research, engineering, product, and business teams.
Ability to travel up to 10%, based on business needs and the clients and industries served.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Preferred Skills:

Research extending tensor networks to applications beyond quantum many-body physics, such as uncertainty quantification, numerical integration, probabilistic graphical models, stochastic processes, differential equations, optimization, or machine learning.
Experience developing new tensor representations, network architectures, contraction algorithms, or methods for controlling approximation error.
Expertise in one or more complementary areas, such as probability and statistics, stochastic modeling, dynamical systems, optimal control, numerical analysis, or computational physics.
Experience with GPU acceleration, parallel computing, or distributed scientific workloads, using tools such as JAX, PyTorch, CUDA, cuTensorNet, MPI, or related technologies.
Experience with scientific tensor software such as Quimb, ITensor, Cotengra, or comparable libraries.
Experience applying computational methods to national security problems, including infrastructure resilience, logistics and supply chains, sensing, materials, or modeling complex systems under uncertainty.
Experience collaborating with government agencies, national laboratories, academic researchers, or multidisciplinary research teams.
Experience developing research proposals, helping define a research agenda, or transitioning research software to broader use.
Familiarity with quantum algorithms or quantum simulation where relevant to the research.

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $134,500 - $265,100.

added.title: Senior Technical Solution Architect
added.description:
About Loop

Loop is industrializing services through AI, starting with one of the world's most complex industries: the global supply chain. We're an AI-native company built to solve the systemic data problem that's held logistics back for decades. Our Logistics Data Platform turns fragmented, unstructured data into a trusted foundation that fuels automation, financial clarity, and decision intelligence at scale.

Our momentum is gaining national recognition. Loop was recently named to LinkedIn's 2026 Top Startups list, ranking #1 in Chicago, #4 in San Francisco, and earning a spot on the national list reflecting our growth, innovation, and the exceptional talent and culture driving our success.

Today, Loop serves >20% of the Fortune 100, manages over $30B in supply chain spend, and helps its clients save hundreds of millions of dollars each year.

We recently closed a $95M Series C and are backed by leading investors including Valor Equity Partners, Founders Fund, 8VC, Index Ventures, J.P. Morgan, and more than 50 industry-leading angel investors.

Our team brings deep expertise from Uber, Google, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Flexport, C3 AI, VMware, Box, UPS, and C.H. Robinson and we're looking for builders who want to help shape what comes next.

About The Role

Technical Solution Architects (TSAs) own the technical side of every customer implementation at Loop: taking a signed enterprise customer from scope to live production, designing how their data lands in Loop, building the integrations and rules their business needs, and leading the cutover. This is an AI-first engineering role: TSAs build and operate the agentic workflows that configure tenants, author rules, validate data, and triage issues, and write the skills, harnesses, and evals that make those agents trustworthy in production, with the explicit goal of automating last quarter's work to take on harder work this quarter. It is also a client-facing delivery role, with technical discovery alongside customer architects and ERP teams, committed go-live dates, and real escalations from some of the largest supply chains in the world. The role sits within Loop's Solution Delivery function, partnering with Implementation Managers, Customer Success, and Product and Engineering, and is distinct from Loop's Forward Deployed Engineering team, which explores zero-to-one product opportunities within Engineering.

This is an in-person role based in San Francisco, CA, with the expectation of being in the office 4+ days per week.

Ability to travel up to 25%.

What You'll Do

Own technical delivery for a portfolio of enterprise customer implementations, from signed scope through production go-live, working to committed dates and go-live gates and holding the quality bar: every implementation validated against real customer data before cutover.
Lead technical discovery with customer stakeholders: turn signed scope into specific, testable requirements, make the design decisions on data model, field mapping, and integration patterns, and partner with Sales and Solutions Engineering on feasibility and effort for non-standard requirements before signature.
Build and operate agentic workflows for delivery: encode implementation know-how as skills and runbooks agents execute, design the harnesses they run in, and write the evals that prove they are correct before they touch production.
Design and build customer integrations: EDI and carrier feeds, SFTP and API ingestion, ERP and payment-system egress (SAP, NetSuite, Oracle, TMS platforms), and custom parsers and transformations for messy real-world data.
Configure the customer's tenant: audit policies, rating and contract logic, cost allocation and GL coding rules, carrier and payee setup, and the cutover from test to production.
Be the technical voice to the customer when things go wrong: diagnose, fix what is configuration, and hand Engineering a clean, reproducible product issue when it is not.
Turn what you learn in the field into product: feed patterns, gaps, and tooling needs back to Product and Engineering so each implementation is faster than the last.

About You

You build with AI agents as a matter of course. You use coding agents daily for real engineering work, and you think in terms of what to delegate, how to structure context and tools so an agent succeeds, and how to verify its output. You can explain where agents fail and what you do about it.
You are a hands-on engineer: TypeScript or Python, SQL, and cloud infrastructure (AWS), with hands-on experience integrating enterprise systems such as ERPs, TMS platforms, EDI, SFTP, and APIs.
You are credible with enterprise customers. You can run a technical call with a customer's architects, push back on scope, and keep a difficult escalation constructive.
You are comfortable owning outcomes with minimal oversight: dates, go-lives, and customers are yours.
You thrive in a role that changes shape. You would rather automate a process and move on than keep doing it by hand.
You communicate clearly in writing and in person, with technical and business audiences alike.

Deep understanding of agentic AI architecture: multi-agent systems, tool use and MCP, context engineering, agent harnesses, evaluation frameworks and evals, prompt and skill design, guardrails, and observability for LLM-driven workflows.
Experience shipping agentic workflows to production and operating them: persistent agents, human-in-the-loop design, and measuring reliability over time.

About Us

Jerry.ai is a Series C, YC-backed tech startup with 5M+ customers and $240M in funding. Founded in 2017, product launched in 2019, and achieved profitability in 2024.

Why We Exist

Your car, home, and motorcycle aren't just purchases, they're the physical embodiment of the life you've worked hard to build. Yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every step of the journey — buying, insuring, maintaining, repairing, selling — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

Imagine having a trusted friend in your pocket who takes care of everything: they find you the right car or home at the right price, lock in the best insurance rate without you lifting a finger, remind you before that service appointment turns into an expensive repair, and help you sell at the best price when the time is right. That friend is Jerry.

We are building the first AI-powered advisor to manage all your physical assets. We started with your car in 2019, now we’re expanding into new verticals (e.g. home, motorcycle, RV, boat).

Why We’re Hiring

Our Data Science & Analytics team has been a force multiplier and accelerant to our business that has helped us reach these pivotal milestones in spite of headwinds and within a highly competitive market. They are a team of former McKinsey, BCG and Bain consultants who drive data & insights, and inform decision-making across every corner of our business. They are analytical powerhouses and first principles problem solvers who push forward our most important initiatives across product, growth, tech, and operations.

Every business unit has a Data Science team member embedded within it — someone who doesn't just run analyses and build dashboards, but shapes what questions we should ask, what data to pull, what conclusions to draw, what decisions to make, and then drives our teams towards our next goal: go from 5M to 50M customers and become a $10B business in the next 4 years.

As Our Business Continues To Expand, There Is Growing Demand For More Data Science Team Members. We Are Hiring 2-3 People To Drive Impact In These Areas

Growth Marketing
Product Development
Strategic Partnerships

On leveling:
You may see job ads for this role at different job levels. Our priority is finding the right people, we can be flexible with job title/leveling.

Why You Will (Or Won't) Like Working Here

No slides: If you've worked in consulting, you know what it feels like to be up at 3am reformatting a deck. That doesn't exist here. The only work that gets done at Jerry is work that will materially change the trajectory of our business — an important product, a new growth channel, a key metric, a critical partner relationship, etc.
No corporate fluff: The Data Science & Analytics team is 14 insatiable learners who care deeply about solving difficult problems and making a tangible impact. Every person owns a critical domain. There is no bloat, unnecessary meetings, or waiting for approvals.
Hands-on: This is not a pure strategy role, you will also own execution. Your day-to-day will be surfacing analytical insights, driving decisions, and seeing them through end-to-end.

What You'll Own

You'll sit on our central Data Science & Analytics team but you’ll be embedded in one of Jerry's core business areas — growth, product, AI and automation, strategic partnerships — and own the analytical function for that business unit end-to-end.

Define the right problems: Before any analysis, understand what business question it's answering and what decision it will inform. Push back if the question is flawed.
Data and insights: Define metrics, build reports, run analyses, design experiments, and surface data insights that move your team's key metrics.
Drive outcomes: Bring recommendations to your counterparts in product, growth, finance or operations, tell them what's happening and why, and what next steps should be.

Who You Are

First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?"
Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.
Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.

2+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.
Strong analytical skills; ability to pull, structure, and interpret data independently.
Track record of owning ambiguous problems and delivering impact.
Clear, persuasive communicator who can influence decisions at the leadership level.

Our Tools

SQL (Clickhouse), Metabase, Python, Jupyter Hub, GitHub.

added.description:
About The Role

Agentic Pods is pioneering a new way for Engineering to partner with teams across Uber and transform how work gets done through AI. Our engineers embed directly with operational teams to understand complex workflows, reimagine what's possible with agentic AI, and build production-grade systems that turn those opportunities into reality.

We are looking for an Agentic Software Engineer to design, build, and operate intelligent, reliable agentic systems that transform complex operational workflows at scale.

This role sits at the intersection of backend engineering, production reliability, and applied AI, combining deep technical ownership with a forward-deployed engineering approach. You'll work closely with operators and domain experts to identify high-impact opportunities, determine where AI agents can safely and effectively improve workflows, and translate ambiguous business challenges into scalable, production-ready solutions.

You'll own the full engineering lifecycle, from problem discovery and system architecture to implementation, deployment, and continuous improvement. This is an opportunity to shape how Uber applies agentic AI to real-world operations while helping establish the technical foundations for broader adoption across the company.

What You'll Do

Design and Build Agentic Systems

Partner directly with operational teams to understand complex workflows, identify inefficiencies, and determine where AI agents, traditional automation, or human decision-making can deliver meaningful improvements.
Design, develop, and deploy production-grade agentic systems, including AI agents, reusable skills, backend services, APIs, system integrations, data pipelines, and human-in-the-loop workflows.
Rapidly prototype, validate, and iterate on solutions with real users, translating ambiguous requirements into reliable, scalable software.

Own Production Reliability and Performance

Design systems with reliability, scalability, and operational resilience in mind, establishing clear performance and quality standards.
Build comprehensive observability across agent behavior, model outputs, system dependencies, and workflow outcomes using tracing, logging, metrics, monitoring, and alerting.
Own systems throughout their production lifecycle, troubleshooting failures, implementing recovery mechanisms, and continuously improving performance based on operational insights and user feedback.

Build Safe, Measurable, and Trustworthy AI Systems

Develop evaluation frameworks to measure agent effectiveness, including task completion, output quality, tool selection, policy compliance, and failure handling.
Implement testing and validation strategies across development, controlled rollouts, and production environments to ensure consistent and predictable system behavior.
Design appropriate safeguards, including access controls, human approvals, auditability, data protection, reversible actions, and escalation mechanisms.
Collaborate with Security, Privacy, Legal, and Data teams to ensure AI-powered workflows meet Uber's standards for safety, compliance, and operational integrity.

Drive Reusability and Engineering Excellence

Identify opportunities to transform individual solutions into reusable agent capabilities, shared services, platform components, and standardized integration patterns.
Design flexible architectures that support different business needs and regional requirements without unnecessary duplication.
Contribute to engineering standards, architecture decisions, development tooling, deployment practices, and reliability frameworks that enable Agentic Pods to scale effectively across Uber.

Who Thrives On This Team

We're looking for engineers who combine strong software engineering fundamentals with curiosity, ownership, and a passion for applying emerging technologies to real-world challenges.

Agentic-first thinker: You see beyond existing workflows and recognize opportunities to fundamentally improve how work gets done using AI and automation.
0→1 builder: You thrive in ambiguous environments and can turn loosely defined problems into working, production-ready solutions.
Product-minded engineer: You focus on solving meaningful user problems and understand that the best solution isn't always the most technically complex.
Systems thinker: You balance immediate business needs with long-term scalability, reliability, and opportunities for reuse.
Collaborative problem solver: You learn unfamiliar domains quickly, build strong relationships with stakeholders, and communicate effectively across technical and non-technical teams.

Minimum Qualifications

PhD or equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field and 2 years of full-time software engineering experience; or 5 years of full-time software engineering experience, including 3 years of specialized technical software engineering experience in one or more programming languages, such as C, C++, Java, Python, or Go.

Note: The 3 years of specialized software engineering experience may be gained through education, full-time employment, additional training, coursework, research, or a combination of these. This experience is not necessarily in addition to the education and full-time work experience requirements listed above.

Strong experience designing, developing, and deploying production backend or distributed systems, such as AI-enabled applications, orchestration platforms, APIs, asynchronous workflows, developer platforms, or enterprise integrations.
Hands-on experience owning production systems, including monitoring, alerting, incident response, troubleshooting, failure recovery, and debugging across application, infrastructure, and data dependencies.
Proficiency in at least one general-purpose programming language, such as Python, Go, Java, or C++.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on experience building agentic AI applications or integrating large language models (LLMs) with tools, APIs, enterprise data sources, and permissioned systems.
Familiarity with agent orchestration, evaluation frameworks, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), context management, model routing, and AI safety controls.
Experience in site reliability engineering (SRE), infrastructure, platform engineering, production engineering, or forward-deployed engineering environments.
Experience designing and operating systems that support sensitive, business-critical, or operationally consequential workflows.
Demonstrated ability to lead technical design, make architectural decisions, and influence engineering direction across teams.
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to collaborate directly with business stakeholders to translate complex operational challenges into technical solutions.

For Seattle, WA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $232,000 per year - USD $258,000 per year.

For Sunnyvale, CA-based roles: The base salary range for this role is USD $232,000 per year - USD $258,000 per year.

For all US locations, you will be eligible to participate in Uber's bonus program, and may be offered an equity award & other types of comp. All full-time employees are eligible to participate in a 401(k) plan. You will also be eligible for various benefits.

Ready to Ride?

This isn't the kind of place where you follow a playbook — it's where you help write one. If you're driven by impact, energized by challenge, and ready to shape how the world moves — we'd love to hear from you.

You may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and other compensation, as well as a range of benefits. Explore our benefits.

added.title: Senior Software Engineer, AI Data
added.description:
NVIDIA is a pioneer in accelerated computing, known for inventing the GPU and driving breakthroughs in gaming, computer graphics, high-performance computing, and artificial intelligence. Our technology powers everything from generative AI to autonomous systems, and we continue to shape the future of computing through innovation and collaboration. Within this mission, our team, Managed AI Research Superclusters (MARS), builds and scales the infrastructure, platforms, and tools that enable researchers and engineers to develop the next generation of AI/ML systems. By joining us, you'll help build solutions that power some of the planet's most advanced computing workloads.

The MARS AI Data team owns how NVIDIA's AI research uses data: many petabytes of training data, checkpoints and datasets across multiple clouds and partners. We build the layer between storage and the workload. That covers data placement across file systems, object storage, and local NVMe. It also includes streaming loaders and caches that supply tens of thousands of GPU cores. Efficient checkpoint management. Quotas remain fair throughout numerous research groups. This is a builder's role on a team that is redefining what it does. You will help design MARS' data platform on Kubernetes from the ground up, working directly with the researchers training NVIDIA's own models. The work shows up as faster training steps, shorter restarts and fewer runs lost to complete storage volumes.

What You'll Be Doing

Design and build the AI data layer for a multi-cloud GPU fleet: how datasets, checkpoints and scratch data are placed, cached, tiered and moved between different storage backends.
Build high-throughput data paths for training and RL. That means streaming loaders from object storage, distributed caches, and checkpoint save and restore at thousands of GPUs, including peer-to-peer and local-first restore.
Make data a first-class part of the compute platform. Build Kubernetes-native APIs, operators and storage integrations so a job declares the data it needs, and the platform mounts, caches and accounts for it, on Slurm and on Kubernetes.
Own quotas, capacity and data lifecycle across hundreds of research teams: usage attribution, quota enforcement, retention, clean-up of stale data, and forecasting capacity before it runs out.
Measure how workloads use data. Build I/O telemetry and access analytics that show hot and cold data, metadata pressure and I/O stalls, and use them to drive placement and fixes.
Own reliability for what you build: on-call, incident analysis, and changes that stop whole classes of data incidents, such as full file systems, runaway metadata load and lost checkpoints.

What We Need To See

BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience.
5+ years building production systems or data-infrastructure software.
Deep experience with at least one of the following: parallel or distributed file systems (Lustre, WEKA, VAST, GPFS, Ceph or similar), object storage at scale (S3 or compatible), or large-scale data pipelines and data lakes.
A clear grasp of I/O performance: throughput, latency, metadata cost, caching and how access patterns interact with each.
Strong programming in Go, Rust, C or C++, plus Python for tooling and analysis.
A track record of owning a service in production and making it measurably better.
Clear written and spoken communication with engineers and researchers.

Ways to stand out from the crowd

Experience feeding large-scale AI training: data loaders, streaming datasets, and storage behavior at thousands of GPUs.
Experience with checkpointing at scale: asynchronous or distributed checkpoints, tiered checkpoint storage, fast restart after failure.
Built or ran a distributed cache or AI-oriented storage system, or used node-local NVMe as a managed tier.
Built a quota, accounting or capacity system that many teams depended on.
Knowledge of RL and agentic workloads and what they need from storage: many small reads, environment snapshots, sandbox images and fast fan-out.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:

152,000 USD – 241,500 USD for Level 3; and 184,000 USD – 287,500 USD for Level 4.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

added.description:
Recognized on the 2025 Forbes Cloud 100 list, ClickHouse is one of the most innovative and fast-growing private cloud companies. With more than 3,000 customers and ARR that has grown over 250 percent year over year, ClickHouse leads the market in real-time analytics, data warehousing, observability, and AI workloads.

The company’s sustained, accelerating momentum was recently validated by a $400M Series D financing round. Over the past three months, customers including Capital One, Lovable, Decagon, Polymarket, and Airwallex have adopted the platform or expanded existing deployments. These customers join an established base of AI innovators and global brands such as Meta, Cursor, Sony, and Tesla.

We’re on a mission to transform how companies use data. Come be a part of our journey!

About The Team

The AI/ML Engineering team builds and operates ClickHouse's AI and machine learning products end-to-end. This includes the Agentic Data Stack, AI Functions, chDB, the in-Console copilot, and the AI/ML partnerships that distribute them — together with the shared components and expertise that let every other ClickHouse team ship AI in the surfaces they own. Our team is looking for highly skilled and experienced software engineers to join us, who will be responsible for designing, building, and operating the products that make ClickHouse the platform of choice for agents and data scientists.

What You Will Do

Feature Development: Design and implement AI-powered features across the full stack, from backend inference services to intuitive frontend interfaces within the ClickHouse Cloud platform.
API Architecture: Create robust, scalable APIs that connect ClickHouse's database capabilities with modern AI/ML inference systems and external/internal AI services.
Ecosystem Integrations: Implement and maintain integrations with the broader AI/ML ecosystem and standards, ensuring that ClickHouse as a technology works seamlessly with popular frameworks and tools.
Technical Integration: Integrate models into production systems with proper monitoring, versioning, observability, and evaluation.
Oncall: Participate in the daytime oncall rotation along with the rest of the team.
ML Engineering: Own the ML pipeline end to end (data, training, evaluation), and fine-tune or train custom models when off-the-shelf ones fall short. Track the state of the art closely enough to apply what genuinely improves our products.

What you will bring along

5+ years of software engineering experience in production environments
Exposure to working directly with AI/ML technologies
Experience integrating and deploying AI/ML models in production systems, including working with inference APIs and vector databases
A high level of ownership and can drive features from concept to production with minimal supervision
Ability to thrive in collaborative environments and can effectively communicate technical concepts to diverse stakeholders
Applied ML experience in Python (Jupyter, PyTorch, common ML libraries), hands-on with compute clusters (Ray, Slurm), and designs trustworthy experiments to drive architectural decisions

Nice to have

Familiarity with cloud technologies such as AWS, Azure, or GCP, particularly services related to AI/ML deployment
Understanding of database systems and data processing pipelines, with ClickHouse experience being a significant plus
Experience with embedding-based systems (retrieval, ranking, recommenders) and the representation-learning ideas underneath them

Perks

Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.
Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.
Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.
Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.
A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.
Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.
