The successful candidate will possess:

Excellent interpersonal and organizational skills, with the ability to handle diverse situations, complex projects, and changing priorities, behaving with passion, empathy, and care.

added.title: Senior Software Engineer, AI Data
added.description:
NVIDIA is a pioneer in accelerated computing, known for inventing the GPU and driving breakthroughs in gaming, computer graphics, high-performance computing, and artificial intelligence. Our technology powers everything from generative AI to autonomous systems, and we continue to shape the future of computing through innovation and collaboration. Within this mission, our team, Managed AI Research Superclusters (MARS), builds and scales the infrastructure, platforms, and tools that enable researchers and engineers to develop the next generation of AI/ML systems. By joining us, you'll help build solutions that power some of the planet's most advanced computing workloads.

The MARS AI Data team owns how NVIDIA's AI research uses data: many petabytes of training data, checkpoints and datasets across multiple clouds and partners. We build the layer between storage and the workload. That covers data placement across file systems, object storage, and local NVMe. It also includes streaming loaders and caches that supply tens of thousands of GPU cores. Efficient checkpoint management. Quotas remain fair throughout numerous research groups. This is a builder's role on a team that is redefining what it does. You will help design MARS' data platform on Kubernetes from the ground up, working directly with the researchers training NVIDIA's own models. The work shows up as faster training steps, shorter restarts and fewer runs lost to complete storage volumes.

What You'll Be Doing

Design and build the AI data layer for a multi-cloud GPU fleet: how datasets, checkpoints and scratch data are placed, cached, tiered and moved between different storage backends.
Build high-throughput data paths for training and RL. That means streaming loaders from object storage, distributed caches, and checkpoint save and restore at thousands of GPUs, including peer-to-peer and local-first restore.
Make data a first-class part of the compute platform. Build Kubernetes-native APIs, operators and storage integrations so a job declares the data it needs, and the platform mounts, caches and accounts for it, on Slurm and on Kubernetes.
Own quotas, capacity and data lifecycle across hundreds of research teams: usage attribution, quota enforcement, retention, clean-up of stale data, and forecasting capacity before it runs out.
Measure how workloads use data. Build I/O telemetry and access analytics that show hot and cold data, metadata pressure and I/O stalls, and use them to drive placement and fixes.
Own reliability for what you build: on-call, incident analysis, and changes that stop whole classes of data incidents, such as full file systems, runaway metadata load and lost checkpoints.

What We Need To See

BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience.
5+ years building production systems or data-infrastructure software.
Deep experience with at least one of the following: parallel or distributed file systems (Lustre, WEKA, VAST, GPFS, Ceph or similar), object storage at scale (S3 or compatible), or large-scale data pipelines and data lakes.
A clear grasp of I/O performance: throughput, latency, metadata cost, caching and how access patterns interact with each.
Strong programming in Go, Rust, C or C++, plus Python for tooling and analysis.
A track record of owning a service in production and making it measurably better.
Clear written and spoken communication with engineers and researchers.

Ways to stand out from the crowd

Experience feeding large-scale AI training: data loaders, streaming datasets, and storage behavior at thousands of GPUs.
Experience with checkpointing at scale: asynchronous or distributed checkpoints, tiered checkpoint storage, fast restart after failure.
Built or ran a distributed cache or AI-oriented storage system, or used node-local NVMe as a managed tier.
Built a quota, accounting or capacity system that many teams depended on.
Knowledge of RL and agentic workloads and what they need from storage: many small reads, environment snapshots, sandbox images and fast fan-out.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:

152,000 USD – 241,500 USD for Level 3; and 184,000 USD – 287,500 USD for Level 4.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 13, 2026.

added.title: Quantum Computing - Senior Applied Research Scientist - Tensor Networks, Research & Delivery _Products & Platforms
added.description:
The Team

Innovation & Delivery Transformation is an organization within Deloitte Consulting that manages a portfolio of emerging technology investments spanning multiple time horizons. Our mission is to accelerate the next generation of technology-driven Consulting offerings. The Quantum Computing team will drive the ecosystem, capability and solution development to drive the impact of quantum technologies across all industries and clients we serve, with the aim of establishing Deloitte as a thought leader and Firm of choice for transformative and disruptive quantum technology.

Position Summary

Do you have a passion for innovation and emerging technologies, along with deep expertise in quantum-inspired algorithms, tensor networks, and high-performance computing? Would you like to be part of the development of a new firm offering? We are currently seeking an experienced Senior Applied Research Scientist - Tensor Networks
to help deliver advanced computational solutions for mission-relevant problems.

As Senior Research Scientist within the Research & Delivery workstream, you will contribute to research and development of advanced computational methods for national security applications. You will investigate how tensor networks can advance modeling, simulation, uncertainty quantification, and decision-making for complex systems. Working with researchers, engineers, and national security specialists, you will translate mission needs into mathematical problems, develop new algorithms, and establish where these methods deliver measurable improvements in accuracy, computational cost, or scale.

You will identify high-value, mission-relevant problems, formulate them for analysis, develop and optimize algorithms, and build rigorous, reproducible benchmarks that distinguish evidence from speculation. You will provide technical contributions to government proposal writing. You will translate validated research into prototypes, reusable software assets, technical roadmaps, and client recommendations while mentoring colleagues and raising standards for technical rigor, reproducibility, and communication.

This role requires candidates to possess or be willing to seek, obtain, and maintain a U.S. government security clearance, as required for the work.

Recruiting for this role ends on 12/31/26.

Work You'll Do

Help build a research practice that extends tensor network methods beyond their established applications to address computational challenges in national security. You will work with researchers, engineers, and mission specialists to identify promising problems, develop new methods, and translate research into capabilities that can be evaluated and used.

Work with national security and domain specialists to translate mission challenges into mathematical models and computational problems. Potential research areas include uncertainty quantification, rare-event analysis, resilient infrastructure and supply chains, probabilistic inference, and dynamical systems.
Determine how dependencies, correlations, network topology, and tensor representations affect computational cost and accuracy. Identify when tensor network approaches are promising and where their limitations arise.
Design, implement, and optimize quantum-inspired algorithms, including tensor network, Pauli-propagation, dequantized, Ising, and QUBO-based methods, using high-performance computing and GPU resources where appropriate.
Collaborate with engineers to improve performance on CPU, GPU, and high-performance computing platforms.
Contribute technical expertise to government proposals and collaborations.
Move validated research from proof of concept to prototype to reusable product assets, including solver and simulator libraries, experiment frameworks, benchmarks, and engineering requirements, in partnership with product and engineering teams.
Serve as technical subject-matter expert in client discussions, executive briefings, proposals, demonstrations, and ecosystem collaborations, clearly communicating results, limitations, uncertainty, and risks.
Mentor researchers and engineers, provide constructive technical review, and establish standards for research rigor, reproducibility, software quality, and communication.
Support work involving government agencies, national laboratories, academic groups, vendors, and other clearance-sensitive stakeholders in accordance with applicable clearance and information-handling requirements.

Required Skills:

Doctoral degree in Physics, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Quantum Information Science, Electrical Engineering, Operations Research, or a related field.
Possess or be willing to seek, obtain, and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.
5+ years of relevant research or development experience, including independently leading technically complex work from problem framing through analysis and communication of conclusions.
Expertise in tensor network methods such as matrix product state (MPS), density matrix renormalization group (DMRG), time-evolving block decimation (TEBD), projected entangled pair states (PEPS), tree tensor networks, or tensor train decompositions, including bond-dimension control, truncation-error analysis, and contraction-path optimization.
Strong foundation in numerical methods, optimization, randomized numerical linear algebra, and quantum-inspired methods for machine learning.
Ability to formulate real-world problems and assess when structural characteristics, such as low entanglement, low rank, sparsity, or operator locality make them suitable for quantum-inspired approaches.
Demonstrated ability to design fair and rigorous benchmarks using strong baselines, appropriate tuning, controlled compute budgets, transparent metrics, and honest reporting of positive and negative results.
Strong Python skills, with experience implementing, reproducing, or critically evaluating algorithms using scientific and quantum software such as NumPy, SciPy, JAX, PyTorch, Quimb, ITensor, Cotengra, Qiskit, Cirq, or PennyLane.
Ability to translate technical research into client-relevant insights, business value, prototypes, roadmaps, or offering priorities.
Publications, preprints, open-source contributions, community benchmarks, conference presentations, or other evidence of technical contribution in quantum-inspired computing, tensor networks, classical simulation, or optimization.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical findings, uncertainty, tradeoffs, and recommendations to technical and business audiences.
Demonstrated ability to guide collaborators, provide constructive technical feedback, and work across research, engineering, product, and business teams.
Ability to travel up to 10%, based on business needs and the clients and industries served.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Preferred Skills:

Research extending tensor networks to applications beyond quantum many-body physics, such as uncertainty quantification, numerical integration, probabilistic graphical models, stochastic processes, differential equations, optimization, or machine learning.
Experience developing new tensor representations, network architectures, contraction algorithms, or methods for controlling approximation error.
Expertise in one or more complementary areas, such as probability and statistics, stochastic modeling, dynamical systems, optimal control, numerical analysis, or computational physics.
Experience with GPU acceleration, parallel computing, or distributed scientific workloads, using tools such as JAX, PyTorch, CUDA, cuTensorNet, MPI, or related technologies.
Experience with scientific tensor software such as Quimb, ITensor, Cotengra, or comparable libraries.
Experience applying computational methods to national security problems, including infrastructure resilience, logistics and supply chains, sensing, materials, or modeling complex systems under uncertainty.
Experience collaborating with government agencies, national laboratories, academic researchers, or multidisciplinary research teams.
Experience developing research proposals, helping define a research agenda, or transitioning research software to broader use.
Familiarity with quantum algorithms or quantum simulation where relevant to the research.

The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Deloitte, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $134,500 - $265,100.

added.title: Biological Data Scientist
added.description:
Current Employees: If you are currently employed at any of the Universities of Wisconsin, log in to Workday to apply through the internal application process.

Job Category:

Academic Staff

Employment Type:

Regular

Job Profile:

Data Scientist I

Job Summary:

We are seeking to hire an experienced research data analyst to support a research program focused on the epidemiology of vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia, led by Dr. Michelle Caunca in the Department of Neurology. The research analyst will be responsible for managing, coordinating, and transforming multiple longitudinal cohort studies. This Data Scientist will support projects focused on biological drivers of vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia, including neuroimaging and blood-based biomarkers.

The analyst will be responsible for developing data management systems and code for merging, harmonizing, and analyzing data that is highly complex in nature. The data in question are complex, longitudinal, and multi-level, including data derived from surveys, laboratory assays, neuroimaging, geocoding, event data, and administrative linkages. The ideal candidate has experience and background in prediction modeling, machine learning, and high-dimensional data analysis.

The position involves managing, analyzing, and interpreting research data from complex cohort studies in R and/or STATA and/or SAS. The successful candidate will have the capacity to manage to optimize reproducibility (including creation of codebooks and reproducible code that can be published), analyze data according to established statistical methods, oversee the work of students and fellow staff (e.g. who may be conducting or interpreting analyses), and develop recommendations based on research findings. The successful candidate will also participate in the preparation of independent and collaborative manuscripts, presentations at academic conferences and to key stakeholders (e.g. community organizations), and in designing analytic plans for future studies.

This position may require some work to be performed in-person, onsite, at a designated campus work location. Some work may be performed remotely, at an offsite, non-campus work location.
Applicants for this position will be considered for the following titles: Data Scientist I, II, or III. The title is determined by the experience and qualifications of the finalist.

Key Job Responsibilities:

Implements appropriate data science techniques under the guidance of other data scientists, statisticians, and/or other researchers to find data patterns and answer research questions chosen by the lead researcher including data visualization, statistical analysis, machine learning, and data mining
Documents approaches to address research questions
Prepares data sets for analysis including cleaning/quality assurance, transformations, restructuring, and integration of multiple data sources
Composes and assembles reproducible workflows and reports to clearly articulate patterns to researchers and/or administrators
Organizes and automates project steps for data preparation and analysis

Department:

School of Medicine and Public Health, Department of Neurology, Caunca Research Lab

added.description:
Who is Saint Louis University? Founded in 1818, Saint Louis University is one of the nation’s oldest and most prestigious Catholic universities. SLU, which also has a campus in Madrid, Spain, is recognized for world-class academics, life-changing research, compassionate health care, and a strong commitment to faith and service.

Job Summary

The Geospatial Research Scientist or Senior Geospatial Research Scientist leads innovative research initiatives in geospatial science, remote sensing, and GeoAI, applying advanced analytics, machine learning, and image processing techniques to address complex challenges in areas such as greenhouse gas emissions, environmental monitoring, and precision agriculture. This position is responsible for developing research concepts, designing and executing experiments, analyzing and integrating multi-source geospatial data, and disseminating findings through publications, presentations, and sponsored research proposals. The Geospatial Research Scientist or Senior Geospatial Research Scientist collaborates with interdisciplinary teams, contributes to strategic partnerships and funding development, and supports the advancement of cutting-edge research within Saint Louis University's Remote Sensing Lab.

Primary Job Responsibilities

Identify compelling scientific questions, design experiments, and conduct ground-breaking research
Participate in securing external funding by developing grant proposals
Liaison to coordinate projects and support interdisciplinary collaboration
Drafting peer-reviewed publications and project reports
Process and analyze drone and satellite data (e.g., WorldView, Planet, SAR)
Participate in field surveys, deploying calibration sites
Performs other duties as assigned

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Strong foundational knowledge in remote sensing, image processing, and geospatial data collection and analysis
Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)
Verbal and written communication skills, including presentations
Strong interpersonal skills, including teamwork and collaboration
Supervisory skills
Ability to integrate interdisciplinary research concepts
Demonstrated ability to collaborate, lead projects, and oversee and guide team members
Proven ability to identify and pursue funding opportunities, developing proposals to secure grants from both academic and industry sources
Expertise in integrating interdisciplinary research concepts to create innovative research applications
Adaptability to work in a dynamic, fast-paced environment, identifying areas for improvement and collaborating with team members to address gaps

Minimum Qualifications For Geospatial Research Scientist

Master’s degree in geospatial science, geography, earth science, or closely related fields such as computer engineering, electronic engineering, computer science, or technology
Three years of related work experience

Preferred Qualifications For Geospatial Research Scientist

Ph.D. in geospatial science, geography or environmental science with geospatial concentration, computer engineering, electronic engineering, geospatial science, earth science or computer science and technology
Strong programming, signal processing, cloud computing, and data analytical skills

Minimum Qualifications For Senior Geospatial Research Scientist

Master’s degree in geospatial science, geography, earth science, or closely related fields such as computer engineering, electronic engineering, computer science, or technology
Five years of related work experience
Project management experience and external engagement
Demonstrated experience in building collaborations, leading projects, and overseeing, and guiding team members

Preferred Qualifications For Senior Geospatial Research Scientist

PhD in geospatial science, geoinformatics, geography, computer science, remote sensing, or related areas with strong geospatial skills
Record of scholarly research and publications

Appointment level will be commensurate with the selected candidate's qualifications and experience. Candidates meeting the qualifications for Senior Geospatial Research Scientist may be appointed at the senior level based on demonstrated research leadership, project management experience, scholarly achievements, and ability to support the growth and strategic objectives of the Remote Sensing Lab.

About The Remote Sensing Lab (rsl)

The Remote Sensing Lab advances geospatial science through machine learning and AI-driven analysis of multi-scale remote sensing data to tackle pressing challenges in food and water security, environmental change, and socio-ecological resilience. Its research combines geospatial computer vision, digital twins and photogrammetry, and sensor fusion—integrating satellite, UAV, and field-based hyperspectral, multispectral, thermal, and LiDAR measurements to monitor agriculture, ecosystems, and land-use dynamics. Active projects span quantum farming and precision agriculture, remote sensing based nitrogen prescriptions to boost crop productivity, early detection of plant diseases, identification of biological and chemical stressors, carbon accounting, permafrost material chemistry, and development of a global InSAR accuracy model. Supported by high-performance computing and advanced imaging systems, the lab delivers innovative GeoAI solutions that drive sustainable agriculture, strengthen food security, and deepen understanding of land-water-climate interactions.

About the job
As an organization, Google maintains a portfolio of research projects driven by fundamental research, new product innovation, product contribution and infrastructure goals, while providing individuals and teams the freedom to emphasize specific types of work. As a Research Scientist, you'll setup large-scale tests and deploy promising ideas quickly and broadly, managing deadlines and deliverables while applying the latest theories to develop new and improved products, processes, or technologies. From creating experiments and prototyping implementations to designing new architectures, our research scientists work on real-world problems that span the breadth of computer science, such as machine (and deep) learning, data mining, natural language processing, hardware and software performance analysis, improving compilers for mobile platforms, as well as core search and much more.

As a Research Scientist, you'll also actively contribute to the wider research community by sharing and publishing your findings, with ideas inspired by internal projects as well as from collaborations with research programs at partner universities and technical institutes all over the world.

The Google Beam team drives world-leading algorithms and system research to power immersive Google Beam telepresence experiences. We develop AI models that synthesize photorealistic 3D views from camera inputs in real time. Our work spans the full research and engineering stack. We focus on reducing hardware complexity, lowering bandwidth requirements, improving robustness, and pushing visual quality enabling Beam products to deliver breakthrough communication experiences that make people feel like they are truly together. Through deep research and rapid prototyping, we de-risk future product directions and build the AI foundations for scalable, accessible 3D telepresence.

At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

Department Summary:

The Trusted Intelligence & Public Safety Software Systems (TIPSS) Department within MITRE Technology and Engineering (MTE) provides technical expertise in support of public safety and national security missions. This position resides in TIPSS and supports work led by the Domestic Security & Strategic Intelligence (DSSI) Division.

TIPSS partners with DSSI departments to bring a multidisciplinary approach to sponsor challenges critical to national security. Its work researches, develops, applies, and accelerates the adoption of advanced capabilities and technologies across law enforcement, analytics, data strategy and management, investigative operations, prototyping, biometrics, and mission solutions.

Position Summary:

MITRE is seeking an Intermediate Data Scientist to help turn large volumes of Department of Justice (DOJ) sponsor data into meaningful insights and actionable recommendations that advance the sponsor’s mission.

Working under the guidance of senior technical staff and in coordination with project leadership, the selected candidate will use hands-on coding and data analysis to investigate mission questions, identify opportunities for improvement, and develop evidence supporting recommended actions. The role includes preparing reproducible analyses, visualizations, models, and presentations that help sponsors understand findings and put recommendations into practice.

The supporting project operates at the intersection of mission, operations, and artificial intelligence. This position offers a recent masters graduate the opportunity to develop technical skills while contributing to real-world mission challenges.

This role requiring on-site presence consistent with corporate policy, between MITRE space and Sponsor space in the District of Columbia. Occasional travel may be required.

Roles & Responsibilities:

Work with senior technical staff and project leadership to understand sponsor needs and translate mission questions into focused analytical tasks.
Use Python, SQL, and related tools to access, clean, combine, and analyze large datasets.
Explore data to identify patterns, trends, and opportunities to improve sponsor capabilities and operations.
Apply statistical methods and develop analytical models, with guidance, to assess findings and support recommendations with sound evidence.
Create visualizations and dashboards using tools such as Power BI to make findings understandable and useful.
Help develop actionable recommendations, assess their expected benefits and limitations, and identify how the sponsor could put them into practice.
Prepare reports and presentations that explain the evidence behind recommendations and help sponsors make informed decisions and adopt improvements.
Maintain organized code, document data sources and analytical methods, and use version control so that analyses can be reviewed, reproduced, and updated.
Participate in peer reviews, incorporate feedback, and communicate progress, questions, and data limitations to the team.
Build familiarity with the sponsor’s mission and relevant technologies in identity management, biometrics, information management, and artificial intelligence.

Basic Qualifications:

U.S. citizenship is required as this position requires having and maintaining a Top-Secret clearance.
Master’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related technical field.
Foundational experience using Python or a comparable programming language for data analysis, demonstrated through coursework, academic projects, internships, research, or personal projects.
Familiarity with SQL and relational databases.
Understanding of basic statistical concepts and methods for exploring, analyzing, and interpreting data.
Ability to communicate analytical findings clearly through writing, visualizations, and presentations.
Organizational skills and attention to detail sufficient to maintain clear documentation and reproducible analytical work.
Ability to work collaboratively, incorporate feedback, and complete assigned tasks under the guidance of experienced staff.
Ability to obtain accounts on the sponsor’s unclassified and classified networks.
Ability to meet on-site requirements consistent with corporate policy and travel occasionally as needed.
No prior full-time professional experience is required.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience in the following areas may be demonstrated through coursework, projects, internships, or undergraduate research:

Using Python and SQL to prepare and analyze data.
Creating dashboards or visualizations in Power BI or Tableau.
Using Git or other version control tools to manage code changes.
Applying statistical or machine learning methods to practical questions and evaluating the reliability of results.
Turning analytical findings into recommendations and presenting the supporting evidence.
Exposure to biometrics, identity matching, name matching, or human-language technologies.

The Trusted Intelligence & Public Safety Software Systems (TIPSS) Department within MITRE Technology and Engineering (MTE) provides technical expertise in support of public safety and national security missions. This position resides in TIPSS and supports work led by the Domestic Security & Strategic Intelligence (DSSI) Division.

TIPSS partners with DSSI departments to bring a multidisciplinary approach to sponsor challenges critical to national security. Its work researches, develops, applies, and accelerates the adoption of advanced capabilities and technologies across law enforcement, analytics, data strategy and management, investigative operations, prototyping, biometrics, and mission solutions.

Position Summary:

MITRE is seeking an Intermediate Data Scientist to help turn large volumes of Department of Justice (DOJ) sponsor data into meaningful insights and actionable recommendations that advance the sponsor’s mission.

Working under the guidance of senior technical staff and in coordination with project leadership, the selected candidate will use hands-on coding and data analysis to investigate mission questions, identify opportunities for improvement, and develop evidence supporting recommended actions. The role includes preparing reproducible analyses, visualizations, models, and presentations that help sponsors understand findings and put recommendations into practice.

The supporting project operates at the intersection of mission, operations, and artificial intelligence. This position offers a recent masters graduate the opportunity to develop technical skills while contributing to real-world mission challenges.

This role requiring on-site presence consistent with corporate policy, between MITRE space and Sponsor space in the District of Columbia. Occasional travel may be required.

Roles & Responsibilities:

Work with senior technical staff and project leadership to understand sponsor needs and translate mission questions into focused analytical tasks.
Use Python, SQL, and related tools to access, clean, combine, and analyze large datasets.
Explore data to identify patterns, trends, and opportunities to improve sponsor capabilities and operations.
Apply statistical methods and develop analytical models, with guidance, to assess findings and support recommendations with sound evidence.
Create visualizations and dashboards using tools such as Power BI to make findings understandable and useful.
Help develop actionable recommendations, assess their expected benefits and limitations, and identify how the sponsor could put them into practice.
Prepare reports and presentations that explain the evidence behind recommendations and help sponsors make informed decisions and adopt improvements.
Maintain organized code, document data sources and analytical methods, and use version control so that analyses can be reviewed, reproduced, and updated.
Participate in peer reviews, incorporate feedback, and communicate progress, questions, and data limitations to the team.
Build familiarity with the sponsor’s mission and relevant technologies in identity management, biometrics, information management, and artificial intelligence.

Basic Qualifications:

U.S. citizenship is required as this position requires having and maintaining a Top-Secret clearance.
Master’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related technical field.
Foundational experience using Python or a comparable programming language for data analysis, demonstrated through coursework, academic projects, internships, research, or personal projects.
Familiarity with SQL and relational databases.
Understanding of basic statistical concepts and methods for exploring, analyzing, and interpreting data.
Ability to communicate analytical findings clearly through writing, visualizations, and presentations.
Organizational skills and attention to detail sufficient to maintain clear documentation and reproducible analytical work.
Ability to work collaboratively, incorporate feedback, and complete assigned tasks under the guidance of experienced staff.
Ability to obtain accounts on the sponsor’s unclassified and classified networks.
Ability to meet on-site requirements consistent with corporate policy and travel occasionally as needed.
No prior full-time professional experience is required.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience in the following areas may be demonstrated through coursework, projects, internships, or undergraduate research:

Using Python and SQL to prepare and analyze data.
Creating dashboards or visualizations in Power BI or Tableau.
Using Git or other version control tools to manage code changes.
Applying statistical or machine learning methods to practical questions and evaluating the reliability of results.
Turning analytical findings into recommendations and presenting the supporting evidence.
Exposure to biometrics, identity matching, name matching, or human-language technologies.

added.description:
Current Employees: If you are currently employed at any of the Universities of Wisconsin, log in to Workday to apply through the internal application process.

Job Profile:

Data Scientist I

Job Summary:

We are seeking to hire an experienced research data analyst to support a research program focused on the epidemiology of vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia, led by Dr. Michelle Caunca in the Department of Neurology. The research analyst will be responsible for managing, coordinating, and transforming multiple longitudinal cohort studies. This Data Scientist will support projects focused on social drivers of vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia.

The analyst will be responsible for developing data management systems and code for merging, harmonizing, and analyzing data that is highly complex in nature. The data in question are complex, longitudinal, and multi-level, including data derived from surveys, laboratory assays, neuroimaging, geocoding, event data, and administrative linkages. The ideal candidate has experience and background in causal inference theory and methodology and social science (e.g. social epidemiology, sociology, demography).

The position involves managing, analyzing, and interpreting research data from complex cohort studies in R and/or STATA and/or SAS. The successful candidate will have the capacity to manage to optimize reproducibility (including creation of codebooks and reproducible code that can be published), analyze data according to established statistical methods, oversee the work of students and fellow staff (e.g. who may be conducting or interpreting analyses), and develop recommendations based on research findings. The successful candidate will also participate in the preparation of independent and collaborative manuscripts, presentations at academic conferences and to key stakeholders (e.g. community organizations), and in designing analytic plans for future studies.

This position may require some work to be performed in-person, onsite, at a designated campus work location. Some work may be performed remotely, at an offsite, non-campus work location.
Applicants for this position will be considered for the following titles: Data Scientist I, II, or III. The title is determined by the experience and qualifications of the finalist.

Key Job Responsibilities:

Documents approaches to address research questions
Organizes and automates project steps for data preparation and analysis
Prepares data sets for analysis including cleaning/quality assurance, transformations, restructuring, and integration of multiple data sources
Implements appropriate data science techniques under the guidance of other data scientists, statisticians, and/or other researchers to find data patterns and answer research questions chosen by the lead researcher including data visualization, statistical analysis, machine learning, and data mining
Composes and assembles reproducible workflows and reports to clearly articulate patterns to researchers and/or administrators

Department:

School of Medicine and Public Health, Department of Neurology, Caunca Research Lab

The Department of Neurology at the University of Wisconsin provides state-of-the-art care for people afflicted with diseases of the nervous system, conducts research in basic and clinical neuroscience, and offers medical students, residents and fellows intensive training in the diagnosis and treatment of neurological disorders. The Department’s mission of clinical service, research and teaching is pursued at the University Hospital, the Middleton Veteran’s Administration Medical Center, the School of Medicine and Public Health, and in a diverse set of clinical outreach sites within the state of Wisconsin. The faculty and academic staff of the department currently consists of over 200 individuals engaged in a broad range of clinical and academic activities. Neurology faculty and academic staff include neurologists, neuropsychologists and scientists who are engaged in basic and clinical research and also contribute to educational programs of the Department. There are more than 32 trainees in a variety of residency, fellowship, and postdoctoral programs.

Compensation:

The starting salary for the position is $60,000 annually for a Data Scientist I, $75,000 annually for a Data Scientist II, and $88,000 annually for a Data Scientist III, but is negotiable based on experience and qualifications.

Employees in this position can expect to receive benefits such as generous vacation, holidays, and sick leave; competitive insurances and savings accounts; retirement benefits. For more information, refer to the campus benefits webpage.

SMPH Faculty /Academic Staff Benefits Flyer 2026

Required Qualifications:

Managing, analyzing, and interpreting research data from complex cohort studies in R and/or STATA and/or SAS.
Manage and analyze data according to established statistical methods, oversee the work of students and fellow staff who also conduct data analysis and develop recommendations based on research findings.
Participate in the preparation of independent and collaborative manuscripts, presentations at academic conferences and to key stakeholders (e.g. community organizations), and in designing subsequent waves of data collection (e.g. via the development of sampling strategies, survey instruments and questionnaires).
Working knowledge of causal inference methods and/or prediction modeling.
Ability to effectively communicate in a team setting.
Ability to write reproducible code, conduct code review, and post code publicly for reproducibility.

Preferred Qualifications:

At least 1-2 years of experience working in an epidemiology or biostatistics group

Education:

Data Scientist I or II: Master's degree in public health, biostatistics, and/or epidemiology or other data science is preferred

Data Scientist III: PhD in public health, biostatistics, and/or epidemiology or other data science is preferred

We are:

A leading partner to the world’s major cloud providers, including AWS, Azure, and Google. The formation of Accenture Cloud First, with a $3 billion investment over three years, demonstrates our commitment to deliver greater value to our clients when they need it most and offers huge growth opportunities for you! Our Cloud First group of more than 70,000 cloud professionals delivers a full stack of integrated cloud capabilities across data, edge, integrated infrastructure and applications, deep ecosystem skills, culture of change along with a deep industry expertise to shape, move, build and operate our clients’ businesses in the cloud. To accelerate our customers transformation leveraging cloud, we combine world-class learning and talent development expertise; deep experience in cloud change management; and cloud-ready operating models with a commitment to responsible business by design — with security, data privacy, responsible use of artificial intelligence, sustainability and ethics and compliance built into the fundamental changes Accenture helps companies achieve.

About the Role: Building the Future in the Age of Agents

Join the elite technical and product engine of the Accenture Google Business Group (AGBG). We are not a traditional project delivery organization; we are a practice of innovators and builders guiding our clients through the most significant shift in technology: the move to Agentic AI and Product-Led Operating Models. As a Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Agentic AI Delivery Engineer, you are a new breed of technologist—a "product-minded engineer" who is as fluent in the language of code as you are in the language of customer outcomes. You don't just build solutions; you leverage the best of technologies Google Cloud has to offer for client requirements, helping clients break free from legacy solution mindset and practices to build truly modern, value-driven software products on Google Cloud.

You Are:

A passionate, hands-on GCP specialist/practitioner who understands that great software is not just about elegant code, but about solving real problems leveraging the best technology tools available for a client. You are as comfortable building a multi-agent workflow on Vertex AI as you are testing a solution built by other team members in a compressed timeline, leveraging the various tools and technologies of Google Cloud. You have a consultative mindset and a deep curiosity to understand the "why" behind a client's business requirements and convert them to an optimal technology solution. You are an evangelist for modern ways of working, grounded in the principles of Product-Led engineering and operating models and related approaches. You are an exceptional communicator, great team player, continuous learner and a true believer in continual change.

The Work:

As a GCP Agentic AI Delivery Engineer, you will be a technical and product-centric engineer in consulting and engineering projects, customizing Google Cloud Agentic solutions for client requirements. You will partner with Accenture's global delivery teams by providing superior technical expertise and product innovation skills. Your role is to execute complex technology solutions for our clients by designing, building, and demonstrating Agentic AI solutions. You will act as a trusted team player, guiding others in the team on how to adopt a Product Engineering mindset and be the expert on specific Google Cloud technologies/products.

Key Responsibilities:

Outcome-Driven Design and Build: Actively participate in technical discovery workshops to translate client business requirements into GCP technology design elements and customized solutions. Design, build, test and deploy innovative, agentic-first solutions on GCP that are directly tied to the client business requirements.

Hands-On Development & Proof-of-Value: Rapidly design, build, and present compelling proof-of-concept (POC) solutions that bring your Google Cloud proficiency to workable solutions. This includes hands-on software engineering using Vertex AI, Gemini/Agentic AI, BigQuery, Google Data technologies, Terraform, and modern CI/CD practices.

Product-Led Project delivery: Act as an agile SME/coach on modern software development. Guide and enable the delivery team on the principles of the Product Agile Operating Model and how to structure delivery sprints for continuous delivery using Google Cloud Technologies.

Team Collaboration: Ability to travel as needed for project meetings, workshops, client discussions, etc., Working with global teams and leveraging the various collaborative tools and channels for project delivery and status reporting.

Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 0 to 100% depending on business need and client requirements.

Here's What You Need

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field or equivalent (minimum 12 years) work experience. (If Associate’s Degree, must have minimum 6 years work experience).

Minimum of 3 years of experience in a hands-on, client-facing technology role (e.g., Google Cloud Engineer, Product Engineer, Technology Consultant).

Minimum of 3 years of deep, hands-on experience architecting and building solutions on GCP.

Minimum of 2 years of experience interacting with project team members distributed across the globe. Well versed in project management methodologies and product/project testing methodologies.

Minimum of 2 years of proven experience on Google Cloud technologies OR Minimum of 1 years of implementation experience on EITHER Agentic systems, leveraging Google Gemini Enterprise, Microsoft Azure Foundry, Microsoft Co-Pilot and/or AWS Bedrock OR on Agentic systems and Google Gemini Enterprise Partner Specialist certifications (CPS)

Bonus points if you have

Product & Agile Mindset: Hands-on experience working within a Product Operating Model. Practical experience in delivering agile projects, contributing to sprint-based deliverables and outcomes.

Consulting & Innovation Acumen: Experience participating in client-facing innovation workshops and converting ideas into outcome-focused solutions. World-class communication skills to articulate project status and delivery challenges and issues to project leadership and client audiences.

Agentic AI & Software Product Engineering: Proven experience architecting and building agentic workflows using Vertex AI. Deep understanding of agentic components, including reasoning engines, planning, tool use, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Hands-on expertise with Google's Gemini models. A commitment to software engineering best practices, including CI/CD, automated testing, and building secure, scalable products.

Technical Depth: Google Cloud Professional certifications (e.g., Professional Cloud Architect, Professional Machine Learning Engineer, Professional Data Engineer, GenAI Leader). Project experience across the GCP ecosystem, including GKE, BigQuery, Vertex AI, CES, Apigee, and other GCP technologies.

added.title: Data Scientist Senior - Model Development
added.description:
Why USAA?

At USAA, our mission is to empower our members to achieve financial security through highly competitive products, exceptional service and trusted advice. We seek to be the #1 choice for the military community and their families.

Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful.

We are proud to support active-duty military spouses. USAA roles may offer remote or hybrid flexibility for active-duty military spouses consistent with applicable policy and business needs.

The Opportunity

As a dedicated Data Scientist Senior you will translate business problems into applied statistical, machine learning, simulation, and optimization solutions to advise actionable business insights and drive business value through automation, revenue generation, and expense and risk reduction. In collaboration with engineering partners, delivers solutions at scale, and enables customer-facing applications. Leverages database, cloud, and programming knowledge to build analytical modeling solutions using statistical and machine learning techniques. Collaborates with other data scientists to improve USAA’s tooling, growing the company’s library of internal packages and applications. Works with model risk management to validate the results and stability of models before being pushed to production at scale.

This role is remote eligible in the continental U.S. with occasional business travel. However, individuals residing within a 60-mile radius of a USAA office will be expected to work on-site.

What You'll Do

Gathers, interprets, and manipulates structured and unstructured data to enable advanced analytical solutions for the business.
Develops scalable, automated solutions using machine learning, simulation, and optimization to deliver business insights and business value.
Selects the appropriate modeling technique and/or technology with consideration to data limitations, application, and business needs.
Develops and deploys models within the Model Development Control (MDC) and Model Risk Management (MRM) framework.
Composes, and assists peers with composing, technical documents for knowledge persistence, risk management, and technical review audiences.
Assesses business needs to propose/recommend analytical and modeling projects to add business value. Works with business and analytics leaders to prioritize analytics and modeling problems/research efforts.
Builds and maintains a robust library of reusable, production-quality algorithms and supporting code, to ensure model development and research efforts are transparent and based on the highest quality data.
Translates complex business request(s) into specific analytical questions, executes on the analysis and/or modeling, and then communicates outcomes to non-technical business colleagues with focus on business action and recommendations.
Manages project milestones, risks, and impediments. Escalates potential issues that could limit project success or implementation.
Develops best practices for engaging with Data Engineering and IT to deploy production-ready analytical assets consistent with modeling best practices and model risk management standards.
Maintains expertise and awareness of cutting-edge techniques. Actively seeks opportunities and materials to learn new techniques, technologies, and methodologies.
Serves as a mentor to junior data scientists in modeling, analytics, and computer science tasks.
Participates in internal communities that drive the maintenance and transformation of data science technologies and culture.
Ensures risks associated with business activities are effectively identified, measured, monitored, and controlled in accordance with risk and compliance policies and procedures.

What You Have

Bachelor’s degree in mathematics, computer science, statistics, economics, finance, actuarial sciences, science and engineering, or other similar quantitative discipline; OR 4 years of experience in statistics, mathematics, quantitative analytics, or related experience (in addition to the minimum years of experience required) may be substituted in lieu of degree.
6 years of experience in a predictive analytics or data analysis OR Advanced Degree (e.g., Master’s, PhD) in mathematics, computer science, statistics, economics, finance, actuarial sciences, science and engineering, or other similar quantitative discipline and 4 years of experience in predictive analytics or data analysis.
4 years of experience in training and validating statistical, physical, machine learning, and other advanced analytics models.
4 years of experience in one or more dynamic scripted language (such as Python, R, etc.) for performing statistical analyses and/or building and scoring AI/ML models.
Proven experience writing code that is easy to follow, well documented, and commented where necessary to explain logic (high code transparency).
Strong experience in querying and preprocessing data from structured and/or unstructured databases using query languages such as SQL, HQL, NoSQL, etc.
Strong experience in working with structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data files such as delimited numeric data files, JSON/XML files, and/or text documents, images, etc.
Demonstrated skill in performing ad-hoc analytics using descriptive, diagnostic, and inferential statistics.
Ability to assess and articulate regulatory implications and expectations of distinct modeling efforts.
Advanced experience with the concepts and technologies associated with classical supervised modeling for prediction such as linear/logistic regression, discriminant analysis, support vector machines, decision trees, forest models, etc.
Advanced experience with the concepts and technologies associated with unsupervised modeling such as k-means clustering, hierarchical/agglomerative clustering, neighbors algorithms, DBSCAN, etc.
Experience guiding and mentoring junior technical staff in business interactions and model building.
Experience communicating analytical and modeling results to non-technical business partners with emphasis on business recommendations and actionable applications of results.

What Sets You Apart

Medium or large bank experience.
Strong knowledge of Python and/or SAS.
Control partner collaboration experience.
Knowledge of Model Risk Management, Model Governance, and Regulatory requirements.

Compensation range:
The salary range for this position is: $143,320-$273,930 .

USAA does not provide visa sponsorship for this role. Please do not apply for this role if at any time (now or in the future) you will need immigration support (i.e., H-1B, TN, STEM OPT Training Plans, etc.).

Compensation:

The Opportunity

As a dedicated Data Scientist Senior you will translate business problems into applied statistical, machine learning, simulation, and optimization solutions to advise actionable business insights and drive business value through automation, revenue generation, and expense and risk reduction. In collaboration with engineering partners, delivers solutions at scale, and enables customer-facing applications. Leverages database, cloud, and programming knowledge to build analytical modeling solutions using statistical and machine learning techniques. Collaborates with other data scientists to improve USAA’s tooling, growing the company’s library of internal packages and applications. Ally Financial only succeeds when its people do - and that’s more than some cliché people put on job postings. We love this stuff! Your hiring manager will discuss this role's specific work requirements with you during the hiring process. All work requirements are subject to change at any time based on leader discretion and/or business need.

The Opportunity

The Senior Specialist - Data Science is responsible for applying advanced data science, machine learning, and Generative AI techniques to solve complex business problems and enable AI-powered capabilities across the enterprise. This role will transform complex data into meaningful insights and develop, evaluate, and deploy analytical and AI solutions that support Ally Vision.

The ideal candidate combines strong expertise in data analysis, statistical methods, machine learning, and programming with experience applying Generative AI and large language models (LLMs) to real-world business problems. This individual will partner closely with business and technology stakeholders to identify opportunities, translate business needs into analytical solutions, and ensure models and AI applications are accurate, scalable, responsible, and effective.

The Work Itself

Data Science & Advanced Analytics: Analyze large and complex datasets using statistical, machine learning, and advanced analytical techniques to identify patterns, generate insights, and solve business problems.
Machine Learning Model Development: Design, develop, evaluate, and optimize machine learning models using appropriate statistical and ML methodologies, including feature engineering, model validation, performance testing, and ongoing monitoring.
Generative AI & LLM Solutions: Develop and evaluate Generative AI solutions using foundation models, including prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), embeddings, semantic search, and agentic AI techniques where appropriate.
Model Evaluation & Experimentation: Develop rigorous evaluation frameworks and experimentation approaches to measure model quality, accuracy, relevance, safety, and business impact. Evaluate alternative approaches and communicate technical trade-offs and recommendations.
Data Preparation & Feature Engineering: Acquire, cleanse, transform, and integrate structured and unstructured data from multiple sources to support analytical modeling and AI solutions.
Productionization & MLOps: Partner with engineering teams to deploy data science and AI solutions into production environments and support model lifecycle management, monitoring, reproducibility, performance optimization, and scalability.
Business Partnership: Collaborate with business and technology partners to define problems, identify appropriate data science approaches, translate analytical findings into actionable recommendations, and communicate complex concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.
Responsible AI & Governance: Apply appropriate controls and governance practices related to model risk, explainability, data privacy, security, bias, and responsible use of AI.
Technical Leadership: Mentor less-experienced data scientists, contribute to technical design and methodology decisions, and help establish reusable data science, machine learning, and AI best practices.

Minimum Qualifications

The Qualifications We’re Looking For
:

3+ years of relevant experience.
Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, or equivalent.

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of experience in data science, machine learning, advanced analytics, or a related quantitative field, with advanced programming skills in Python and common data science/ML libraries.
Master's degree in relevant quantitative discipline.
Experience with SQL and large, complex datasets, including preparing, transforming, and analyzing structured and unstructured data.

Experience with data science and machine learning frameworks such as scikit-learn, PyTorch, or TensorFlow, as well as integrating internally hosted or third-party foundation models.
Experience working within AWS, Azure, or GCP, with familiarity deploying analytical, machine learning, or AI solutions and applying MLOps/LLMOps practices such as monitoring, versioning, reproducibility, and observability.
Knowledge of Responsible AI, model governance, data privacy, security, and appropriate handling of sensitive data and PII.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to translate complex analytical findings into meaningful business insights and provide technical guidance to other data scientists or analysts.

added.description:
The Team

Innovation & Delivery Transformation is an organization within Deloitte Consulting that manages a portfolio of emerging technology investments spanning multiple time horizons. Our mission is to accelerate the next generation of technology-driven Consulting offerings. The Quantum Computing team will drive the ecosystem, capability and solution development to drive the impact of quantum technologies across all industries and clients we serve, with the aim of establishing Deloitte as a thought leader and Firm of choice for transformative and disruptive quantum technology.

Position Summary

Do you have a passion for innovation and emerging technologies, along with deep expertise in quantum-inspired algorithms, tensor networks, and high-performance computing? Would you like to be part of the development of a new firm offering? We are currently seeking an experienced Senior Applied Research Scientist - Tensor Networks
to help deliver advanced computational solutions for mission-relevant problems.

As Senior Research Scientist within the Research & Delivery workstream, you will contribute to research and development of advanced computational methods for national security applications. You will investigate how tensor networks can advance modeling, simulation, uncertainty quantification, and decision-making for complex systems. Working with researchers, engineers, and national security specialists, you will translate mission needs into mathematical problems, develop new algorithms, and establish where these methods deliver measurable improvements in accuracy, computational cost, or scale.

You will identify high-value, mission-relevant problems, formulate them for analysis, develop and optimize algorithms, and build rigorous, reproducible benchmarks that distinguish evidence from speculation. You will provide technical contributions to government proposal writing. You will translate validated research into prototypes, reusable software assets, technical roadmaps, and client recommendations while mentoring colleagues and raising standards for technical rigor, reproducibility, and communication.

This role requires candidates to possess or be willing to seek, obtain, and maintain a U.S. government security clearance, as required for the work.

Recruiting for this role ends on 12/31/26.

Work You'll Do

Help build a research practice that extends tensor network methods beyond their established applications to address computational challenges in national security. You will work with researchers, engineers, and mission specialists to identify promising problems, develop new methods, and translate research into capabilities that can be evaluated and used.

Work with national security and domain specialists to translate mission challenges into mathematical models and computational problems. Potential research areas include uncertainty quantification, rare-event analysis, resilient infrastructure and supply chains, probabilistic inference, and dynamical systems.
Determine how dependencies, correlations, network topology, and tensor representations affect computational cost and accuracy. Identify when tensor network approaches are promising and where their limitations arise.
Design, implement, and optimize quantum-inspired algorithms, including tensor network, Pauli-propagation, dequantized, Ising, and QUBO-based methods, using high-performance computing and GPU resources where appropriate.
Collaborate with engineers to improve performance on CPU, GPU, and high-performance computing platforms.
Contribute technical expertise to government proposals and collaborations.
Move validated research from proof of concept to prototype to reusable product assets, including solver and simulator libraries, experiment frameworks, benchmarks, and engineering requirements, in partnership with product and engineering teams.
Serve as technical subject-matter expert in client discussions, executive briefings, proposals, demonstrations, and ecosystem collaborations, clearly communicating results, limitations, uncertainty, and risks.
Mentor researchers and engineers, provide constructive technical review, and establish standards for research rigor, reproducibility, software quality, and communication.
Support work involving government agencies, national laboratories, academic groups, vendors, and other clearance-sensitive stakeholders in accordance with applicable clearance and information-handling requirements.

Required Skills:

Doctoral degree in Physics, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Quantum Information Science, Electrical Engineering, Operations Research, or a related field.
Possess or be willing to seek, obtain, and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.
5+ years of relevant research or development experience, including independently leading technically complex work from problem framing through analysis and communication of conclusions.
Expertise in tensor network methods such as matrix product state (MPS), density matrix renormalization group (DMRG), time-evolving block decimation (TEBD), projected entangled pair states (PEPS), tree tensor networks, or tensor train decompositions, including bond-dimension control, truncation-error analysis, and contraction-path optimization.
Strong foundation in numerical methods, optimization, randomized numerical linear algebra, and quantum-inspired methods for machine learning.
Ability to formulate real-world problems and assess when structural characteristics, such as low entanglement, low rank, sparsity, or operator locality make them suitable for quantum-inspired approaches.
Demonstrated ability to design fair and rigorous benchmarks using strong baselines, appropriate tuning, controlled compute budgets, transparent metrics, and honest reporting of positive and negative results.
Strong Python skills, with experience implementing, reproducing, or critically evaluating algorithms using scientific and quantum software such as NumPy, SciPy, JAX, PyTorch, Quimb, ITensor, Cotengra, Qiskit, Cirq, or PennyLane.
Ability to translate technical research into client-relevant insights, business value, prototypes, roadmaps, or offering priorities.
Publications, preprints, open-source contributions, community benchmarks, conference presentations, or other evidence of technical contribution in quantum-inspired computing, tensor networks, classical simulation, or optimization.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical findings, uncertainty, tradeoffs, and recommendations to technical and business audiences.
Demonstrated ability to guide collaborators, provide constructive technical feedback, and work across research, engineering, product, and business teams.
Ability to travel up to 10%, based on business needs and the clients and industries served.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Preferred Skills:

Research extending tensor networks to applications beyond quantum many-body physics, such as uncertainty quantification, numerical integration, probabilistic graphical models, stochastic processes, differential equations, optimization, or machine learning.
Experience developing new tensor representations, network architectures, contraction algorithms, or methods for controlling approximation error.
Expertise in one or more complementary areas, such as probability and statistics, stochastic modeling, dynamical systems, optimal control, numerical analysis, or computational physics.
Experience with GPU acceleration, parallel computing, or distributed scientific workloads, using tools such as JAX, PyTorch, CUDA, cuTensorNet, MPI, or related technologies.
Experience with scientific tensor software such as Quimb, ITensor, Cotengra, or comparable libraries.
Experience applying computational methods to national security problems, including infrastructure resilience, logistics and supply chains, sensing, materials, or modeling complex systems under uncertainty.
Experience collaborating with government agencies, national laboratories, academic researchers, or multidisciplinary research teams.
Experience developing research proposals, helping define a research agenda, or transitioning research software to broader use.
Familiarity with quantum algorithms or quantum simulation where relevant to the research.

Join the elite technical and product engine of the Accenture Google Business Group (AGBG). A passionate, hands-on GCP specialist/practitioner who understands that great software is not just about elegant code, but about solving real problems leveraging the best technology tools available for a client. You are as comfortable building a multi-agent workflow on Vertex AI as you are testing a solution built by other team members in a compressed timeline, leveraging the various tools and technologies of Google Cloud. You are an evangelist for modern ways of working, grounded in the principles of Product-Led engineering and operating models and related approaches. You are an exceptional communicator, great team player, continuous learner and a true believer in continual change.

Product-Led Project delivery: Act as an agile SME/coach on modern software development. Guide and enable the delivery team on the principles of the Product Agile Operating Model and how to structure delivery sprints for continuous delivery using Google Cloud Technologies.

Team Collaboration: Ability to travel as needed for project meetings, workshops, client discussions, etc., Working with global teams and leveraging the various collaborative tools and channels for project delivery and status reporting.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field or equivalent (minimum 12 years) work experience. (If Associate’s Degree, must have minimum 6 years work experience).

Air Force Civilian Service, we don’t just support the mission — we help shape the future of national defense through discovery, innovation, and unwavering dedication.

The Air Force Civilian Service (AFCS) is looking for a full-time Enterprise Artificial Intelligence (AI) Services Lead (GS-1515/1550-14), working at the Secretary of the Air Force (SAF), Chief Data Office, in the National Capital Region, Joint Base Andrews, in Camp Springs, Maryland.

This is an interdisciplinary position and may be filled in operations research or computer science. The incumbent must meet the educational requirements below; for Ops Research OR Computer Science.

Salary ($143,913 - $187,093) based on experience.

Depending on the type of position (competitive/excepted) you are selected for, you will be required to serve a 1-year probationary period OR 2-year trial period.

This position can close at any time. Apply Now!

Qualifications/Requirements

In this position you will serve as an Enterprise AI Services Lead. You will be tasked to lead the functional management office for all Department of the Air Force (DAF) enterprise AI services, and you are responsible for ensuring the delivery of robust, scalable, and secure AI capabilities to meet mission needs across the Total Force. This role requires a technical and programmatic leader focused on operationalizing AI solutions, managing the enterprise AI ecosystem, and driving the DAF's digital transformation through the adoption of cutting-edge AI services and infrastructure.

Must be a U.S. Citizen

Must be able to obtain & maintain a “Top Secret” Security clearance.

This position is designated as a Drug Test Designated Position

Education Operations Research (1515)

This position requires a degree in operations research; OR at least 24 semester hours in a combination of operations research, mathematics, probability, statistics, mathematical logic, science, or subject-matter courses requiring substantial competence in college-level mathematics or statistics. At least 3 of the 24 semester hours must have been in calculus.

Education Computer Science (1550)

This position requires at least a bachelor’s degree in computer science OR bachelor's degree with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of the 30 semester hours must have included any combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus. All academic degrees and course work must be from accredited or pre-accredited institutions.

Service Management: Leads the functional management, design, and architecture of the DAF enterprise AI infrastructure. Apply computer science principles to theoretical models for the representations and transformations of information structures and software configuration. Models and frames scenarios that are meaningful and impact critical operational or business processes.
AI Operationalization: Drives the operationalization of AI by working with mission owners to identify, prioritize, and implement enterprise-level AI solutions. Leads discovery processes with stakeholders to identify requirements. Provides technical guidance and analyzes problems to advise on the feasibility of different approaches for the solution to a specific problem.
Capability Delivery: Oversees the development and management of the enterprise AI ecosystem, including common pipelines for developing, testing, and deploying AI models. Apply analysis and quantification skills to develop innovative approaches to solve analytics problems. Plans, designs, and conducts tests to obtain data.
Program Advocacy: Serves as a key proponent for advancing AI, advocating for high-priority enterprise use cases that deliver transformational change. Serves as an authority and consultant to other organizations. Promotes interchange of information on mission requirements, capabilities, and technology applications. Represents the organization with government and industry.
Tasker Response: Responds to internal and external taskers regarding enterprise AI services, infrastructure, and capabilities. Serves as an authority and consultant. Provides professional and technical advice to high-level officials.

Plans and executes major projects to support organization objectives. About The Position

AWS Solutions Architect

﻿Location: US / Canada (Eastern Time) - Home based

Job Type: Full-time, Permanent

About AllCloud

AllCloud helps organizations get more from the cloud through AI-led professional and managed services. We are an AWS Premier Tier Services Partner with audited Managed Services, and a Salesforce Consulting Partner. We have delivered hundreds of migrations and implementations, and our Engage Managed Services support customers from first migration through ongoing operations. We serve clients worldwide from offices in North America and EMEA.

As a Delivery Solutions Architect, you are the technical lead on customer engagements. You own the technical vision and the SOW’s technical deliverables, and you lead the Cloud Engineers who build them. You’ll be the customer’s trusted technical advisor, connecting their business goals to the architecture and making sure what we deliver meets both. Most of the work is on-prem-to-AWS migrations and new AWS architectures, with a growing share of GenAI workloads. You use coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex every day to move faster and raise quality.

Requirements

What You’ll Do

Own the technical vision and architecture for each engagement, from kickoff to handover
Own the SOW’s technical deliverables, scope and requirements, and flag risk or scope changes early
Lead and mentor the project’s Cloud Engineers: set direction, review designs and code, unblock the team
Be the customer’s trusted technical advisor, from engineers up to IT leadership
Turn business and application requirements into technical designs and delivery plans
Lead on-prem and data center migrations to AWS: discovery, wave planning, cutover
Design and build new AWS architectures, including GenAI workloads (e.g. Amazon Bedrock)
Use coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) for IaC, automation, documentation and delivery acceleration
Apply AWS Well-Architected principles to every design: security, reliability, performance, cost
Work with PMs, managed services and sales; support scoping of follow-on work when needed
Build reusable assets and reference architectures, and share them across the practice

What You Bring

8+ years in enterprise IT, including 5+ years hands-on in software development, DevOps, systems engineering or architecture
Proven delivery of production AWS solutions, especially large migrations
Experience leading technical teams on customer-facing projects
Depth in at least two of: infrastructure/networking, security, databases/data, containers/serverless
Hands-on IaC (Terraform or CDK/CloudFormation) and CI/CD
Daily, practical use of AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex or similar)
Exposure to GenAI on AWS (Bedrock, RAG, agents)
Confident with customer stakeholders, from engineers to executives
Strong written communication: designs, runbooks, status updates and handover docs

Nice to Have

AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional (required within 2 months if not held)
AWS Generative AI Developer – Professional or Machine Learning Engineer – Associate
Experience with AWS MAP-funded migrations
A degree in Computer Science or a related technical field

Why work for us?

Our team inspires progress in each other and in our customers through our relentless pursuit of excellence; you will work with leaders who promote learning and personal development.
